explanation: S3 scales infinitely without management and Intelligent-Tiering automatically optimizes costs based on access patterns. EBS requires manual scaling and has 64TB limit per volume. EFS is expensive at PB scale. FSx doesn't auto-scale to PB levels efficiently.

text: A real-time analytics platform ingests 100TB daily with requirements for immediate querying of recent data and long-term archival. Which storage design optimizes for both access patterns?
options: S3 Standard for all data with Athena queries
S3 Express One Zone for hot data, S3 Glacier for archives
Redshift with local SSD and Spectrum for S3 data
EBS io2 for hot data, S3 for cold data
explanation: S3 Express One Zone provides single-digit millisecond latency for frequently accessed data while S3 Glacier handles cost-effective archival. Standard S3 alone has higher latency for real-time queries. Redshift with Spectrum is complex for this volume. EBS doesn't scale efficiently to 100TB daily.

text: An application experiences throttling when accessing S3 with 10,000 requests per second to the same prefix. Which optimization strategies improve performance? (Select TWO)
options: Implement random prefix naming for object keys
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration
Use CloudFront for GET requests
Implement exponential backoff only
Enable S3 request metrics
explanation: Random prefixes distribute load across S3 partitions preventing hotspots. CloudFront caches frequently accessed objects reducing S3 load. Transfer Acceleration helps with uploads, not request rate. Exponential backoff handles throttling but doesn't prevent it. Metrics help monitoring but don't improve performance.

text: A financial application requires 80,000 IOPS for its database with ability to scale to 200,000 IOPS within minutes during trading hours. Which EBS configuration meets this requirement?
options: gp3 with baseline 16,000 IOPS and burst capability
io2 with 80,000 provisioned IOPS and elastic volumes
io1 with 64,000 IOPS and additional volumes when needed
gp2 with credit accumulation for burst performance
explanation: io2 supports up to 256,000 IOPS with elastic volumes feature allowing dynamic IOPS increases without downtime. gp3 maxes at 16,000 IOPS. io1 is limited to 64,000 IOPS. gp2 burst is unpredictable and limited to 3,000 IOPS.

text: A machine learning team needs shared storage for training data (100TB) accessible from both Linux and Windows instances with SMB and NFS protocols. Which solution provides the required compatibility?
options: EFS with NFS mount for Linux, SMB not supported
FSx for NetApp ONTAP with multi-protocol access
FSx for Windows File Server with NFS client
S3 with File Gateway providing both protocols
explanation: FSx for NetApp ONTAP natively supports both NFS and SMB protocols, allowing simultaneous access from Linux and Windows. EFS only supports NFS. FSx Windows primarily supports SMB. File Gateway requires separate gateways for each protocol.

text: An application requires temporary storage with 3.3 million IOPS for data processing. Processed results must be stored permanently. Which combination provides optimal performance? (Select TWO)
options: Instance store for temporary processing
EBS io2 Block Express for temporary storage
S3 for permanent storage of results
EFS for both temporary and permanent storage
DynamoDB for permanent results storage
explanation: Instance store can provide millions of IOPS for temporary processing on certain instance types (i3, i4i). S3 provides durable, scalable storage for permanent results. EBS io2 maxes at 256,000 IOPS. EFS isn't optimized for this IOPS level. DynamoDB is a database, not general storage.

text: A content management system requires shared file storage for 10,000 concurrent users with low latency for metadata operations. The workload is read-heavy with occasional writes. Which EFS configuration is optimal?
options: General Purpose performance mode with Elastic throughput
Max I/O performance mode with Provisioned throughput
General Purpose with Bursting throughput
Max I/O with Elastic throughput
explanation: General Purpose mode provides lowest latency for metadata operations crucial for many concurrent users. Elastic throughput auto-scales based on workload. Max I/O has higher latency. Bursting may not sustain 10,000 users. Provisioned requires capacity planning.

text: An application stores 1PB of genomic data with 80% rarely accessed. Researchers need sub-second access when data is requested. Which S3 storage configuration optimizes cost and performance?
options: S3 Standard for all data
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval for all data
S3 Intelligent-Tiering with Archive Instant Access tier
S3 Standard-IA with lifecycle to Glacier
explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between access tiers. Archive Instant Access tier provides sub-second retrieval at lower cost than Standard-IA. Standard is expensive for 1PB. Glacier Instant for all data doesn't optimize frequently accessed portion. Standard-IA to Glacier loses instant access.

text: A Windows-based enterprise application requires 10GB/s throughput with Active Directory integration and data deduplication. Which storage solution meets all requirements?
options: FSx for Windows File Server with SSD storage
FSx for Lustre with Windows compatibility layer
EFS with Windows NFS client
FSx for NetApp ONTAP with CIFS shares
explanation: FSx for Windows File Server provides native Windows compatibility, AD integration, and data deduplication with SSD storage supporting up to 12.5 GB/s throughput. FSx Lustre doesn't integrate with AD. EFS requires third-party NFS clients on Windows. ONTAP is more complex for pure Windows workloads.

text: A high-performance computing cluster needs scratch storage with 1TB/s aggregate throughput for temporary simulation data. Cost is critical as data doesn't need persistence. Which solution is MOST cost-effective?
options: FSx for Lustre scratch filesystem
Instance store across multiple instances
EBS io2 volumes in RAID 0
S3 with parallel uploads
explanation: FSx Lustre scratch filesystem is designed for temporary HPC workloads with up to 1TB/s throughput at lower cost than persistent options. Instance store requires complex coordination. EBS io2 is expensive and persistent. S3 has higher latency for HPC scratch needs.

text: A video streaming platform needs to serve millions of users globally. Original 8K videos (50GB each) need transcoding to multiple formats. Which architecture optimizes storage and delivery? (Select THREE)
options: S3 for original video storage with lifecycle policies
CloudFront for global content delivery
EFS for transcoded video storage
S3 Intelligent-Tiering for transcoded formats
Instance store for temporary transcoding workspace
explanation: S3 stores original videos durably with lifecycle management. CloudFront provides global edge delivery. Intelligent-Tiering optimizes storage costs for multiple formats with varying access patterns. Instance store provides high-performance temporary workspace. EFS is expensive for video storage at scale.

text: A financial firm requires storage for trading data with 100μs latency, 1 million IOPS, and real-time replication to DR site. Which architecture meets these extreme requirements?
options: Instance store with application-level replication
EBS io2 Block Express with DRS
FSx for NetApp ONTAP with SnapMirror
S3 Express One Zone with CRR
explanation: Instance store on specialized instances (i4i) can achieve 100μs latency and millions of IOPS. Application-level replication handles DR. EBS has higher latency. FSx ONTAP can't achieve 100μs latency. S3 Express still has millisecond latency.

text: A data lake built on S3 experiences slow query performance with Athena. Data is stored in CSV format with daily partitions. Which optimizations provide the BEST performance improvement? (Select TWO)
options: Convert data to Parquet format
Implement hourly partitions instead of daily
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration
Compress files with GZIP
Increase Athena result cache size
explanation: Parquet is columnar format optimized for analytics queries. GZIP compression reduces data scanned improving performance and cost. Hourly partitions may create too many small files. Transfer Acceleration doesn't help query performance. Result cache size doesn't affect initial query performance.

text: A legacy application requires block storage with 15,000 IOPS but cannot be modified to use multiple volumes. The solution must be cost-optimized. Which option meets these requirements?
options: Single gp3 volume with 15,000 IOPS provisioned
Single io2 volume with 15,000 IOPS
Single gp2 volume with sufficient size for burst
Multiple gp3 volumes with RAID controller
explanation: gp3 supports up to 16,000 IOPS at lower cost than io2. Single volume meets the legacy app requirement. io2 is more expensive for this IOPS level. gp2 can't sustain 15,000 IOPS. RAID requires application changes.

text: An e-commerce platform needs to scale storage from 10TB to 100TB during Black Friday. Post-event, storage should scale down. Which solutions provide elastic scaling? (Select TWO)
options: S3 with no configuration changes needed
EFS with automatic scaling
EBS with elastic volumes feature
FSx with manual capacity adjustment
Aurora storage auto-scaling
explanation: S3 scales infinitely without configuration. EFS automatically scales capacity up and down based on data stored. EBS elastic volumes only scales up, not down. FSx requires manual intervention. Aurora is database, not general storage.

text: A containerized application needs persistent storage that can be dynamically provisioned by Kubernetes with specific IOPS requirements. Which solution provides the BEST integration?
options: EFS with CSI driver and access points
EBS with CSI driver and storage classes
Instance store with StatefulSets
S3 with S3 CSI driver
explanation: EBS CSI driver integrates with Kubernetes storage classes allowing dynamic provisioning with specific IOPS through gp3/io2 volumes. EFS CSI works but doesn't provide IOPS guarantees. Instance store isn't persistent. S3 CSI is not standard for block storage needs.

text: A machine learning workload requires 96 vCPUs, 768 GiB memory, and 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs for training models. Cost optimization is important but not critical. Which instance type is MOST appropriate?
options: p4d.24xlarge with On-Demand pricing
p3.16xlarge with Spot instances
g4dn.metal with Reserved Instances
inf1.24xlarge with Savings Plans
explanation: p4d.24xlarge provides 96 vCPUs, 1152 GiB memory, and 8 A100 GPUs meeting all requirements. p3 has older V100 GPUs. g4dn has T4 GPUs unsuitable for heavy ML training. inf1 is for inference, not training.

text: An application requires consistent network performance of 25 Gbps with SR-IOV support for low-latency trading. Which instance family provides these capabilities at lowest cost?
options: M5n instances with Enhanced Networking
C5n instances with Elastic Network Adapter
T3 instances with placement groups
R5 instances with dedicated hosts
explanation: C5n instances provide up to 100 Gbps network performance with ENA and SR-IOV support, optimized for network-intensive workloads. M5n offers up to 25 Gbps but C5n is more cost-effective for network-focused needs. T3 doesn't support SR-IOV. R5 is memory-optimized, not network-optimized.

text: A web application experiences traffic patterns: baseline 100 RPS, daily peaks at 9 AM (500 RPS), and unpredictable viral spikes up to 5000 RPS. Which Auto Scaling configuration optimizes cost and performance?
options: Target tracking on CPU with 40% target
Scheduled scaling for morning peak, target tracking for spikes
Step scaling with aggressive thresholds
Simple scaling with cooldown periods
explanation: Scheduled scaling proactively handles predictable 9 AM peaks. Target tracking dynamically responds to viral spikes. This combination minimizes costs during low traffic while ensuring capacity. Pure target tracking lags for scheduled peaks. Step and simple scaling are less responsive.

text: An Auto Scaling group must maintain exactly 6 instances across 3 AZs for quorum requirements. During AZ failure, the application needs redistribution without exceeding 6 total instances. Which configuration achieves this?
options: Min: 6, Max: 6, Desired: 6 with AZ rebalancing enabled
Min: 2, Max: 8, Desired: 6 with capacity rebalancing
Min: 6, Max: 9, Desired: 6 with termination protection
Min: 6, Max: 6, Desired: 6 with suspend AZ rebalancing
explanation: Setting Min/Max/Desired all to 6 maintains exactly 6 instances. AZ rebalancing redistributes instances across healthy AZs during failure without exceeding max capacity. Other options either allow capacity changes or don't handle AZ failures properly.

text: A Lambda function processes images with execution times varying from 100ms to 5 minutes based on image complexity. Memory usage peaks at 8GB. Which configuration optimizes performance and cost?
options: 3008 MB memory with 5-minute timeout
10240 MB memory with 15-minute timeout
1024 MB memory with Step Functions for orchestration
8192 MB memory with 6-minute timeout
explanation: 8192 MB provides required memory with 6-minute timeout covering max execution time. Higher memory also provides more CPU for faster processing. 3008 MB insufficient for 8GB peaks. 10240 MB wastes resources. Step Functions adds unnecessary complexity.

text: An event-driven application needs to process 100,000 concurrent requests with sub-second response time. Each request requires 512MB memory. Which serverless solution is MOST suitable?
options: Lambda with reserved concurrency of 100,000
Fargate with ECS service auto-scaling
Lambda with provisioned concurrency
App Runner with automatic scaling
explanation: Lambda with provisioned concurrency eliminates cold starts ensuring sub-second responses. Reserved concurrency doesn't prevent cold starts. Fargate has longer startup times. App Runner is for web apps, not event-driven processing.

text: A microservices application requires Kubernetes-native deployment with managed control plane, GPU support for ML services, and Windows container support. Which solution meets ALL requirements?
options: EKS with managed node groups and mixed instance types
ECS with EC2 launch type and GPU instances
EKS with self-managed nodes on multiple instance types
ECS with Fargate and GPU support
explanation: EKS with managed node groups supports Kubernetes-native deployments, GPU instances for ML, and Windows containers on Windows node groups. Self-managed requires more overhead. ECS isn't Kubernetes-native. Fargate doesn't support GPUs.

text: A containerized application needs to scale from 10 to 10,000 containers based on queue depth. The application is stateless with unpredictable traffic. Which configuration provides best elasticity? (Select TWO)
options: ECS with Fargate and Service Auto Scaling
EKS with Cluster Autoscaler and HPA
ECS on EC2 with capacity providers
Lambda with SQS triggers
Batch with managed compute environment
explanation: Fargate with Service Auto Scaling provides serverless container scaling without managing infrastructure. EKS with Cluster Autoscaler (nodes) and HPA (pods) enables Kubernetes-native scaling. EC2 requires capacity management. Lambda limited to 15-minute execution. Batch is for batch processing.

text: A genomics company needs to process 10,000 analysis jobs nightly. Each job requires 16 vCPUs for 2-6 hours. Cost optimization is critical. Which solution is MOST cost-effective?
options: AWS Batch with Spot compute environment
ECS with scheduled Fargate tasks
Lambda with Step Functions orchestration
EMR with transient clusters
explanation: AWS Batch with Spot instances provides up to 90% cost savings for batch workloads. It handles job scheduling, Spot interruptions, and automatic retries. Fargate is more expensive. Lambda has 15-minute limit. EMR is for big data analytics.

text: An organization runs monthly financial reports requiring 1000 parallel jobs with dependencies. Jobs must complete within 8-hour window. Which service provides the required orchestration?
options: AWS Batch with job queues and array jobs
Step Functions with parallel states
SWF with custom deciders
Lambda with SQS FIFO queues
explanation: AWS Batch handles complex job dependencies, array jobs for parallelization, and automatic resource provisioning. Step Functions has limits on parallel executions. SWF requires custom implementation. Lambda/SQS doesn't handle dependencies natively.

text: A company needs to run Apache Spark jobs processing 100TB daily. The cluster should auto-scale based on workload and minimize costs. Which EMR configuration is optimal?
options: EMR on EC2 with managed scaling and Spot instances
EMR on EKS with Kubernetes autoscaling
EMR Serverless with automatic scaling
EMR on Outposts for dedicated capacity
explanation: EMR Serverless automatically scales resources based on job requirements without managing clusters, optimizing costs for variable workloads. EMR on EC2 requires cluster management. EMR on EKS adds Kubernetes complexity. Outposts is for on-premises requirements.

text: A data pipeline needs to process streaming data with Apache Flink, store results in S3, and query with Presto. Which architecture provides best integration?
options: Kinesis Analytics for Flink, S3, and Athena
EMR with Flink, S3, and Presto applications
Lambda for stream processing, S3, and Redshift
Glue Streaming ETL with S3 and Athena
explanation: EMR supports Flink, Presto, and other big data tools in a single cluster with S3 integration through EMRFS. Kinesis Analytics doesn't support Presto. Lambda isn't suitable for Flink. Glue Streaming doesn't provide Flink.

text: A global application needs to execute code at edge locations for sub-10ms latency. The code modifies HTTP headers and performs A/B testing. Which solution is MOST appropriate?
options: Lambda@Edge with CloudFront
Lambda with API Gateway edge-optimized endpoints
EC2 instances in Local Zones
Outposts with Application Load Balancer
explanation: Lambda@Edge runs code at CloudFront edge locations providing sub-10ms latency for header manipulation and A/B testing. API Gateway edge doesn't run code at edge. Local Zones aren't globally distributed. Outposts is for on-premises.

text: An IoT application needs to process data from 1 million devices with 5ms latency requirements in major cities. Which edge computing solution meets these requirements? (Select TWO)
options: AWS Local Zones for ultra-low latency
AWS Wavelength for 5G networks
CloudFront for edge caching
Global Accelerator for routing
IoT Greengrass for edge processing
explanation: Local Zones provide single-digit millisecond latency in metro areas. Wavelength enables ultra-low latency on 5G networks. CloudFront is for content delivery. Global Accelerator improves routing but doesn't provide edge compute. Greengrass is for IoT devices.

text: A SaaS platform needs to scale different application tiers independently based on: web tier (CPU), app tier (memory), and cache tier (network). Which scaling strategy is MOST appropriate?
options: Single Auto Scaling group with mixed instance types
Separate Auto Scaling groups with tier-specific metrics
AWS Auto Scaling with scaling plans
Manual scaling based on CloudWatch dashboards
explanation: Separate Auto Scaling groups allow independent scaling policies based on tier-specific metrics (CPU, memory, network). Single group couples all tiers. Auto Scaling plans are for predictive scaling. Manual scaling isn't elastic.

text: A fault-tolerant batch processing system needs to minimize costs using Spot instances while maintaining availability. Which strategy provides best reliability?
options: Single instance type in one AZ
Multiple instance types across multiple AZs
Spot blocks for defined duration
Spot Fleet with lowest price strategy
explanation: Diversifying across multiple instance types and AZs reduces interruption risk when specific Spot capacity becomes unavailable. Single type/AZ has high interruption risk. Spot blocks are deprecated. Lowest price strategy doesn't optimize availability.

text: A video processing pipeline has stages with different processing times: upload (1s), transcode (5min), thumbnail (30s), notify (100ms). How should compute be decoupled for optimal scaling? (Select TWO)
options: SQS queues between each stage
Lambda for short tasks, ECS for long tasks
Step Functions for workflow orchestration
All stages in single ECS task
Kinesis streams for all stages
explanation: SQS queues decouple stages allowing independent scaling. Lambda handles short tasks (upload, thumbnail, notify) while ECS handles long transcoding. Step Functions adds orchestration overhead. Single task prevents independent scaling. Kinesis is for streaming.

text: An e-commerce platform needs to decouple order processing from inventory updates. Orders must process in sequence per customer but parallel across customers. Which pattern is MOST suitable?
options: SQS FIFO with message group ID per customer
SNS with SQS fan-out pattern
Kinesis with partition key per customer
EventBridge with rule-based routing
explanation: SQS FIFO with message group IDs ensures order sequence per customer while allowing parallel processing across different customers. SNS fan-out doesn't guarantee order. Kinesis requires more complex consumer logic. EventBridge is for event routing, not sequencing.

text: A Lambda function experiences cold starts affecting user experience. The function has 3GB memory and receives 100 concurrent requests during business hours. Which optimization is MOST effective?
options: Increase memory to 10GB for faster initialization
Enable provisioned concurrency for business hours
Reduce deployment package size
Implement Lambda SnapStart
explanation: Provisioned concurrency keeps functions initialized during business hours, eliminating cold starts for predictable traffic. More memory doesn't eliminate cold starts. Package size helps but doesn't eliminate the issue. SnapStart is for Java functions.

text: An application on t3.large instances experiences CPU credit depletion during sustained loads. The workload requires consistent performance. Which solution is MOST appropriate?
options: Enable T3 Unlimited mode
Switch to M5 instances
Purchase more CPU credits
Add more T3 instances
explanation: M5 instances provide consistent performance without credit system, suitable for sustained workloads. T3 Unlimited incurs extra charges. CPU credits can't be purchased directly. More T3 instances still face credit issues.

text: A real-time analytics platform processes 1 million events/second with requirements: <100ms processing latency, exactly-once processing, and auto-scaling based on stream volume. Which architecture meets ALL requirements?
options: Kinesis Data Streams → Lambda → DynamoDB
Kinesis Data Streams → Kinesis Analytics → S3
MSK → Flink on EMR → OpenSearch
SQS FIFO → Lambda → RDS
explanation: MSK with Flink provides exactly-once processing guarantees, sub-100ms latency, and auto-scaling capabilities. Lambda has cold starts affecting latency. Kinesis Analytics has limited exactly-once support. SQS FIFO has throughput limitations.

text: A multi-tenant SaaS needs compute isolation per tenant with ability to scale from 0 to 1000 concurrent executions. Each execution runs for 30 seconds. Which solution provides best isolation and elasticity? (Select TWO)
options: Lambda with reserved concurrency per tenant
Fargate with separate task definitions per tenant
EKS with namespace per tenant
Batch with job queue per tenant
EC2 with dedicated instances per tenant
explanation: Lambda reserved concurrency provides compute isolation and scales to 1000 executions. Fargate task definitions ensure container isolation with serverless scaling. EKS namespaces provide logical, not compute isolation. Batch is for batch processing. Dedicated instances are costly.

text: An HPC cluster needs 500 instances with 100Gbps network, EFA support, and cluster placement for tightly-coupled MPI workloads. Which configuration provides optimal performance?
options: C5n.18xlarge with cluster placement group and EFA
M5zn.12xlarge with spread placement group
R5n.24xlarge with partition placement group
Hpc6a.48xlarge with cluster placement group and EFA
explanation: Hpc6a.48xlarge is purpose-built for HPC with 100Gbps EFA networking and optimized for tightly-coupled workloads. C5n.18xlarge has 100Gbps but Hpc6a offers better price-performance. M5zn lacks EFA. R5n is memory-optimized, not HPC-optimized.

text: A financial application requires ACID compliance, complex JOINs across 50 tables, stored procedures, and 50,000 IOPS. The database must support automatic failover. Which solution is MOST appropriate?
options: DynamoDB with global tables
Aurora MySQL with Multi-AZ
DocumentDB with read replicas
Neptune with multi-region replication
explanation: Aurora MySQL provides ACID compliance, supports complex JOINs and stored procedures, delivers up to 200,000 IOPS, and includes automatic Multi-AZ failover. DynamoDB is NoSQL without JOIN support. DocumentDB is for document workloads. Neptune is for graph databases.

text: An e-commerce platform needs a database supporting 10 million read requests/second with microsecond latency for shopping cart data. Write consistency can be eventual. Which solution provides the required performance?
options: RDS with read replicas
DynamoDB with DAX caching
ElastiCache Redis as primary datastore
Aurora Global Database
explanation: DynamoDB with DAX provides microsecond latency for millions of requests/second through in-memory caching. RDS can't achieve microsecond latency. ElastiCache alone lacks persistence guarantees. Aurora has millisecond, not microsecond latency.

text: A global application has users in 5 regions with a read-heavy workload (95% reads). The application requires <100ms read latency globally and strong consistency for financial transactions. Which architecture is optimal?
options: Aurora Global Database with up to 5 secondary regions
RDS Multi-AZ with cross-region read replicas
DynamoDB Global Tables with consistent reads
Single region Aurora with CloudFront caching
explanation: Aurora Global Database supports up to 5 secondary regions with <1 second replication lag and local read latency. Primary region handles writes with strong consistency. RDS cross-region replicas have higher lag. DynamoDB Global Tables use eventual consistency. CloudFront can't cache dynamic database queries.

text: An analytics workload requires 15 read replicas for different reporting teams. The replicas need different instance sizes based on query complexity. Which database supports this requirement?
options: RDS MySQL with 15 read replicas
Aurora MySQL with 15 Aurora Replicas
RDS PostgreSQL with cascading replicas
DocumentDB with 15 read replicas
explanation: Aurora supports up to 15 Aurora Replicas with independent instance sizes for different workload requirements. RDS supports maximum 5 read replicas (15 with cascading but complex). DocumentDB supports 15 replicas but isn't ideal for analytics.

text: An application experiences database bottlenecks with 80% cache hit ratio. Analysis shows stale cache entries causing data inconsistency. Which caching strategy resolves both performance and consistency issues? (Select TWO)
options: Implement write-through caching with ElastiCache
Use lazy loading with shorter TTL values
Deploy write-around pattern with cache invalidation
Add more cache nodes for higher memory
Implement cache-aside with versioning
explanation: Write-through ensures cache consistency by updating cache on writes. Cache-aside with versioning prevents stale data through version checks. Lazy loading doesn't address consistency. Write-around still has stale data risk. More nodes don't fix consistency.

text: A DynamoDB table experiences throttling despite provisioned capacity of 10,000 RCU/WCU. Investigation reveals hot partition keys. Which solution provides the BEST performance improvement?
options: Increase table capacity to 20,000 RCU/WCU
Enable auto-scaling with target utilization 70%
Redesign partition key for better distribution
Switch to on-demand billing mode
explanation: Redesigning partition key for even distribution eliminates hot partitions, allowing full capacity utilization. Increasing capacity doesn't fix hot partition issue. Auto-scaling doesn't resolve partition-level throttling. On-demand still throttles hot partitions.

text: An OLTP database requires 60,000 Provisioned IOPS with consistent performance. The database size is 10TB. Which configuration provides the required performance?
options: RDS MySQL with Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) - 60,000 IOPS
Aurora MySQL with standard storage
RDS PostgreSQL with General Purpose SSD (gp3) - 16,000 IOPS
Aurora PostgreSQL with I/O-Optimized configuration
explanation: Aurora I/O-Optimized provides predictable pricing and performance for I/O-intensive workloads, easily supporting 60,000+ IOPS. RDS io1 maxes at 40,000 IOPS (or 80,000 for Nitro). Standard Aurora charges per I/O. gp3 maxes at 16,000 IOPS.

text: A serverless application using Lambda experiences connection exhaustion with RDS MySQL during traffic spikes. The database supports 1,000 connections. Which solution BEST resolves this issue?
options: Increase RDS instance size for more connections
Implement RDS Proxy for connection pooling
Use DynamoDB instead of RDS
Add read replicas to distribute connections
explanation: RDS Proxy pools and reuses database connections, solving Lambda's connection multiplication issue. Larger instance has connection limits. DynamoDB requires application rewrite. Read replicas don't solve connection pooling.

text: A company migrates from Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL. The application uses stored procedures, triggers, and Oracle-specific SQL syntax. Which approach minimizes migration effort?
options: AWS DMS with SCT for heterogeneous migration
Direct dump and restore with manual conversion
AWS DataSync for database files transfer
Babelfish for Aurora PostgreSQL
explanation: DMS with Schema Conversion Tool handles heterogeneous migrations, automatically converting Oracle objects to PostgreSQL equivalents. Direct dump requires extensive manual conversion. DataSync is for files, not databases. Babelfish is for SQL Server compatibility.

text: A startup needs a relational database that scales from zero during off-hours to handle 100,000 concurrent connections during viral events. Cost optimization is critical. Which solution is MOST appropriate?
options: Aurora Serverless v1 with auto-pause
Aurora Serverless v2 with minimum 0.5 ACU
RDS with scheduled scaling
Aurora Standard with reader auto-scaling
explanation: Aurora Serverless v2 scales from 0.5 ACU (minimal cost) to maximum capacity instantly, handling 100,000+ connections. v1 has scaling limitations and pause delays. RDS scheduled scaling can't handle viral spikes. Standard Aurora has fixed costs.

text: An IoT application writes 1M records/second with queries for device data from the last 7 days. Older data is rarely accessed but must be retained for compliance. Which architecture optimizes cost and performance?
options: DynamoDB with TTL and backup to S3
Timestream with automatic data tiering
RDS with partitioning by date
Kinesis Data Firehose to S3 with Athena
explanation: Timestream is purpose-built for time-series data with automatic tiering between memory (recent) and magnetic (historical) storage. Handles 1M writes/second efficiently. DynamoDB expensive for this volume. RDS can't handle write rate. Firehose+Athena has query latency.

text: A social media platform needs to store user profiles (structured), posts (semi-structured), and relationship graphs. Each data type has different access patterns. Which combination provides optimal performance? (Select TWO)
options: DynamoDB for user profiles with consistent structure
DocumentDB for flexible post schemas
Neptune for social graph relationships
Single Aurora database with JSON columns
Elasticsearch for all data types
explanation: DynamoDB excels at structured key-value access for profiles. Neptune is purpose-built for graph traversals in social relationships. DocumentDB works for posts but Neptune better for relationships. Single Aurora not optimized for graph queries. Elasticsearch is for search, not primary storage.

text: An application requires global secondary indexes, point-in-time recovery, and encryption at rest. The workload is unpredictable with peaks of 40,000 RCU. Which configuration is MOST cost-effective?
options: DynamoDB provisioned with auto-scaling
DynamoDB on-demand mode
Aurora with read replicas
DocumentDB with elastic clusters
explanation: DynamoDB on-demand handles unpredictable workloads cost-effectively, supporting up to 40,000 RCU peaks without pre-provisioning. Supports GSI, PITR, and encryption. Provisioned with auto-scaling has lag and waste. Aurora/DocumentDB don't have GSI concept.

text: A financial application requires in-memory caching with ACID transactions and immediate consistency. The cache must survive instance failures. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: ElastiCache Redis with AOF persistence
MemoryDB for Redis with Multi-AZ
ElastiCache Memcached with multiple nodes
DynamoDB with DAX caching
explanation: MemoryDB provides ACID transactions with immediate consistency and Multi-AZ durability for instance failures. ElastiCache Redis has eventual consistency with AOF. Memcached doesn't support persistence. DAX is eventually consistent.

text: A blockchain analytics platform needs to query relationships between millions of wallet addresses with 6-degree traversals. Queries must complete in seconds. Which database provides optimal performance?
options: Neptune with Gremlin queries
DynamoDB with adjacency list pattern
DocumentDB with graph lookups
RDS with recursive CTEs
explanation: Neptune is purpose-built for graph databases, optimized for traversing relationships efficiently. 6-degree traversals complete in seconds. DynamoDB adjacency lists inefficient for deep traversals. DocumentDB not optimized for graphs. RDS recursive CTEs very slow for large graphs.

text: An e-commerce platform needs: product catalog (complex queries), shopping cart (session data), order history (time-series), and recommendations (graph). Which architecture provides optimal performance?
options: Single Aurora cluster with different schemas
DynamoDB for all with different partition strategies
Purpose-built databases: Aurora, ElastiCache, Timestream, Neptune
DocumentDB with different collections
explanation: Purpose-built databases optimize each workload: Aurora for complex SQL queries, ElastiCache for session management, Timestream for time-series orders, Neptune for graph-based recommendations. Single database compromises performance. DynamoDB not optimal for complex queries or graphs.

text: A multi-tenant SaaS requires database isolation per tenant with ability to scale from 10 to 10,000 tenants. Each tenant has 1-100GB data. Which strategy provides best isolation and scalability? (Select TWO)
options: Aurora with schema per tenant
DynamoDB with partition key per tenant
Aurora with database per tenant using RDS Proxy
Separate AWS account per tenant with DynamoDB
Single DynamoDB table with tenant-id prefix
explanation: Database per tenant in Aurora with RDS Proxy provides strong isolation while managing connections efficiently. Separate accounts with DynamoDB provides strongest isolation for large tenants. Schema per tenant harder to manage at scale. Single table risks noisy neighbor. Partition key alone insufficient isolation.

text: An Aurora database shows high replica lag during peak hours affecting read consistency. Write throughput is 50,000 writes/second. Which optimization provides the MOST improvement?
options: Enable Aurora parallel query
Switch to Aurora Global Database
Enable write forwarding on replicas
Implement Aurora I/O-Optimized storage
explanation: Aurora I/O-Optimized improves replication performance for high write throughput workloads, reducing replica lag. Parallel query is for analytical queries. Global Database for multi-region. Write forwarding doesn't reduce lag.

text: A data warehouse experiences slow query performance on 10TB dataset. Queries scan entire tables for aggregations. Which optimization strategies provide best improvement? (Select TWO)
options: Migrate to Redshift with distribution keys
Implement Redshift materialized views
Add more RDS read replicas
Increase Aurora instance size
Use Redshift Spectrum for cold data
explanation: Redshift with proper distribution keys optimizes data placement for query patterns. Materialized views pre-compute aggregations improving performance. Read replicas don't help single query performance. Instance size has limits. Spectrum for external data, not primary optimization.

text: A gaming application requires consistent network performance with 40ms or less latency globally for UDP traffic. The application cannot use HTTP/HTTPS protocols. Which AWS service provides optimal performance?
options: CloudFront with custom origins
Global Accelerator with Network Load Balancer endpoints
Route 53 with latency-based routing
Elastic Load Balancer with cross-zone balancing
explanation: Global Accelerator uses AWS global network infrastructure to optimize TCP/UDP traffic routing with anycast IP addresses, reducing latency by up to 60%. CloudFront is for HTTP/HTTPS content delivery. Route 53 provides DNS routing but doesn't optimize network paths. ELB is regional, not global.

text: A media streaming platform needs to deliver video content globally with adaptive bitrate streaming. Content includes live streams and 100TB of on-demand videos. The solution must support custom HTTP headers for analytics. Which architecture optimizes global delivery?
options: Global Accelerator with custom HTTP headers
CloudFront with Lambda@Edge for header manipulation
Direct S3 distribution with Transfer Acceleration
Regional CDNs with Route 53 geo-routing
explanation: CloudFront provides global edge locations for video delivery with caching capabilities, while Lambda@Edge enables custom header manipulation for analytics at the edge. Global Accelerator doesn't support custom headers for HTTP. S3 Transfer Acceleration doesn't provide edge caching. Regional CDNs lack AWS integration benefits.

text: A three-tier web application in a VPC requires separation between web, application, and database layers with internet access only for the web tier. The database tier needs outbound internet access for updates. Which subnet design provides optimal security and functionality?
options: Public subnets for all tiers with security groups
Public subnet for web tier, private subnets for app/database tiers with NAT Gateway
Private subnets for all tiers with VPC endpoints
Public subnets for web/app, private subnet for database
explanation: Public subnet for web tier enables direct internet access, private subnets for app/database tiers provide security isolation, and NAT Gateway allows secure outbound internet access for database updates. All public subnets reduce security. All private subnets prevent web tier internet access. Mixed public for web/app doesn't isolate application tier properly.

text: A company needs to design network addressing for a VPC that will host 500 EC2 instances across 3 availability zones, with room for 100% growth. Each AZ should have equal capacity and support both public and private subnets. Which CIDR allocation strategy is most efficient?
options: VPC: 10.0.0.0/16, each AZ gets /18 (16,384 IPs)
VPC: 10.0.0.0/20, each AZ gets /22 (1,024 IPs)
VPC: 10.0.0.0/22, each AZ gets /24 (256 IPs)
VPC: 10.0.0.0/24, each AZ gets /26 (64 IPs)
explanation: VPC /16 provides 65,536 IPs total. Each AZ getting /18 provides 16,384 IPs (8,192 per public/private subnet), easily accommodating 334 instances per AZ with 100% growth capacity. /20 provides only 4,096 total IPs (insufficient for 1,000 instances). /22 and /24 provide even less capacity.

text: A multi-tier application requires routing traffic between tiers with specific path-based routing rules. Web tier (/) routes to app servers, API calls (/api/*) route to microservices, and admin panel (/admin/*) routes to management servers. Which routing architecture provides the required functionality? (Select TWO)
options: Application Load Balancer with listener rules
Network Load Balancer with target groups
Route 53 with weighted routing policies
CloudFront with behavior patterns
API Gateway with custom domain
Classic Load Balancer with sticky sessions
explanation: Application Load Balancer supports path-based routing with listener rules for /api/* and /admin/* patterns. CloudFront behaviors can route different paths to different origins (/admin/* to management servers, /api/* to microservices). Network Load Balancer doesn't support path-based routing. Route 53 provides DNS routing, not HTTP path routing. API Gateway is for APIs, not general web routing.

text: Which action is MOST appropriate for securing the AWS account root user?
options: Attach a full-access policy for break-glass
Create access keys for automation
Enable MFA and avoid using root for daily operations
Rotate the root password weekly and share among admins
explanation: Root should have MFA enabled and be used only for tasks that require it; no access keys for root.

text: A financial trading application requires sticky sessions for user state management, SSL termination, and the ability to route based on custom HTTP headers. The application experiences traffic bursts of 100,000 requests per second. Which load balancer configuration provides optimal performance?
options: Application Load Balancer with session affinity and custom routing rules
Network Load Balancer with TCP sticky sessions
Classic Load Balancer with cookie-based stickiness
Gateway Load Balancer with flow hash algorithm
explanation: Application Load Balancer supports all requirements: session affinity (sticky sessions), SSL termination, custom header routing, and can handle high request volumes with auto-scaling. Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 without HTTP header awareness. Classic Load Balancer is deprecated and has lower performance limits. Gateway Load Balancer is for network appliances, not application traffic.

text: A gaming platform needs to distribute player connections across game servers based on geographic location and current server load. Players use persistent TCP connections that should maintain connection to the same server for the entire gaming session. Which load balancing strategy optimizes player experience?
options: Application Load Balancer with geographic routing
Network Load Balancer with flow hash algorithm
Global Accelerator with health-based routing
Route 53 with geolocation routing to regional NLBs
explanation: Route 53 geolocation routing directs players to their nearest region, while Network Load Balancers maintain persistent TCP connections with flow hash for session persistence. ALB is for HTTP traffic. NLB alone doesn't provide geographic routing. Global Accelerator optimizes paths but doesn't provide geographic server selection.

text: A microservices architecture has 50 different services with varying traffic patterns. Some services receive 10 RPS while others handle 10,000 RPS. The solution must support service discovery, health checks, and cross-zone load balancing. Which load balancing architecture provides optimal resource utilization?
options: Single Application Load Balancer with multiple target groups
Individual Network Load Balancers per service
Application Load Balancer with AWS App Mesh integration
Classic Load Balancers with Auto Scaling groups
explanation: ALB with App Mesh provides efficient load balancing across services with service mesh benefits: service discovery, health checks, and traffic management. Single ALB is cost-effective but lacks service mesh features. Individual NLBs per service are expensive and over-engineered. Classic Load Balancers are deprecated and less efficient.

text: An application requires load balancing for both HTTP/HTTPS web traffic and TCP database connections. The web traffic needs content-based routing while database connections require connection persistence. Which combination provides optimal performance? (Select TWO)
options: Application Load Balancer for HTTP traffic
Network Load Balancer for database connections
Classic Load Balancer for both traffic types
Gateway Load Balancer for database security
Route 53 health checks for failover
CloudFront for database connection caching
explanation: Application Load Balancer optimally handles HTTP/HTTPS with content-based routing capabilities. Network Load Balancer provides low-latency TCP load balancing with connection persistence for database traffic. Classic Load Balancer can't efficiently handle both requirements. Gateway Load Balancer is for network appliances. Route 53 provides DNS services. CloudFront doesn't cache database connections.

text: A financial institution requires 10Gbps dedicated connectivity between their on-premises data center and AWS with consistent latency under 5ms. The connection must support multiple VPCs and provide backup connectivity. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Site-to-Site VPN with multiple tunnels
Direct Connect with Virtual Interfaces
VPN over Direct Connect for redundancy
AWS PrivateLink with Interface Endpoints
explanation: Direct Connect provides dedicated 10Gbps connectivity with consistent low latency. Virtual Interfaces (VIFs) enable connection to multiple VPCs. BGP routing provides path redundancy. Site-to-Site VPN has variable latency over internet. VPN over DX adds unnecessary complexity. PrivateLink is for accessing AWS services, not general connectivity.

text: A company needs to connect 20 branch offices to AWS with encrypted connectivity. Each office has 50-100Mbps internet connection and requires access to VPC resources. The solution must be cost-effective and easy to manage. Which architecture provides optimal connectivity?
options: Direct Connect with hosted connections per office
Site-to-Site VPN with Customer Gateways
AWS Client VPN with individual certificates
Transit Gateway with VPN attachments
explanation: Transit Gateway with VPN attachments provides centralized connectivity management for multiple sites, cost-effective scaling, and simplified routing. Single DX per office is expensive. Individual Site-to-Site VPNs create complex mesh topology. Client VPN is for individual users, not site connectivity.

text: A multinational corporation operates in 8 regions globally with requirements for inter-region communication, centralized security policies, and disaster recovery failover. Each region has 3 VPCs (prod, staging, dev). Which network topology provides optimal global connectivity?
options: VPC Peering mesh between all VPCs
Transit Gateway in each region with TGW Peering
AWS Global Network with Direct Connect
Route 53 with health check failover
explanation: Transit Gateway per region simplifies VPC connectivity within each region, while TGW Peering provides inter-region communication with centralized routing policies. VPC Peering mesh becomes unmanageable (168 connections needed). Global Network isn't a connectivity service. Route 53 provides DNS services, not network connectivity.

text: A hybrid architecture requires seamless connectivity between on-premises (10.0.0.0/8), AWS production VPCs (172.16.0.0/12), and AWS development VPCs (192.168.0.0/16) across 3 regions. The solution must prevent production-development cross-talk while allowing on-premises access to both. Which design optimizes security and connectivity?
options: Single Transit Gateway with route tables
Separate Transit Gateways for prod/dev with shared connection
VPC Peering with filtered route tables
Direct Connect to each VPC individually
explanation: Separate Transit Gateways for production and development provide network isolation while shared Direct Connect Virtual Interface enables on-premises access to both environments through routing policies. Single TGW risks cross-environment traffic. VPC Peering creates complex routing. Individual DX connections are expensive and complex to manage.

text: A SaaS platform expects to grow from 10 customers to 10,000 customers over 2 years. Each customer requires network isolation and 1Gbps bandwidth. The current architecture uses separate VPCs per customer. Which scaling strategy accommodates future growth?
options: Continue VPC-per-customer with increased limits
Transit Gateway with customer-specific route tables
Multi-tenant VPC with customer-specific subnets
Separate AWS accounts per customer
explanation: Separate AWS accounts provide strongest isolation with native billing separation and account-level resource limits, scaling to thousands of customers. VPC limits (1000 per account) insufficient for 10,000 customers. Transit Gateway route tables have limits. Multi-tenant VPC risks noisy neighbor issues and complex security.

text: A content delivery platform needs to serve 10PB of video content globally with 99.99% availability. Peak traffic reaches 100Gbps in multiple regions simultaneously. Which network architecture provides optimal global distribution?
options: Regional S3 buckets with cross-region replication
CloudFront with multiple origin failover
Global Accelerator with Network Load Balancer
Multi-region deployment with Route 53 failover
explanation: CloudFront provides global edge locations for video content delivery with massive scale capacity (>100Gbps), multiple origin failover for 99.99% availability, and intelligent routing. Regional S3 doesn't provide edge caching globally. Global Accelerator optimizes TCP/UDP, not content delivery. Route 53 alone doesn't provide content caching.

text: A real-time multiplayer game requires consistent 20ms latency globally for UDP traffic with 50,000 concurrent players. The game cannot tolerate packet loss or latency spikes during traffic bursts. Which combination optimizes network performance? (Select TWO)
options: Global Accelerator for path optimization
CloudFront for content caching
Network Load Balancer with flow hash
Enhanced networking on EC2 instances
Placement groups for low latency
Route 53 latency-based routing
explanation: Global Accelerator uses AWS backbone to optimize UDP traffic paths globally, reducing latency by up to 60%. Network Load Balancer with flow hash maintains connection persistence for gaming sessions while handling burst traffic. CloudFront is for HTTP content. Enhanced networking helps locally but not globally. Placement groups are for same-AZ resources.

text: A financial trading system requires deterministic network latency under 100μs between application tiers within the same availability zone. The application processes 5 million transactions per second with microsecond-sensitive timing. Which network configuration achieves optimal performance?
options: Enhanced networking with SR-IOV enabled
Cluster placement group with 100Gbps networking
Single-root I/O virtualization (SR-IOV) instances
Dedicated hosts with enhanced networking
explanation: Cluster placement groups provide single-digit microsecond network latency between instances in the same AZ with 100Gbps network performance, optimal for latency-sensitive trading applications. Enhanced networking alone doesn't guarantee cluster placement. SR-IOV is enabled by default on modern instances. Dedicated hosts don't improve network latency between instances.

text: A data analytics platform processes 100TB datasets across 1000 EC2 instances with shuffle operations requiring high inter-instance bandwidth. The workload is compute-intensive and network-bound. Which network optimization strategy provides maximum throughput?
options: 100Gbps Enhanced Networking with placement groups
Multiple Elastic Network Interfaces per instance
Network Load Balancer for traffic distribution
Dedicated bandwidth with Reserved Instances
explanation: 100Gbps Enhanced Networking with cluster placement groups maximizes inter-instance bandwidth for shuffle-heavy workloads, providing line-rate performance between instances. Multiple ENIs don't increase total bandwidth per instance. NLB distributes external traffic, not inter-instance communication. Reserved Instances provide cost savings, not bandwidth increases.

text: A enterprise application requires a four-tier architecture: web (public), application (private), database (private), and management (isolated). Each tier needs different security policies and network access patterns. Which network design provides optimal security and operational efficiency?
options: Four separate VPCs with VPC peering
Single VPC with four subnet tiers and security groups
Transit Gateway with shared services VPC
Multi-account setup with cross-account roles
explanation: Single VPC with subnet tiers provides efficient routing and cost-effectiveness while security groups and NACLs enforce tier-specific policies. Separate VPCs add complexity without security benefits. Transit Gateway adds unnecessary overhead. Multi-account is overkill for tier separation.

text: A microservices platform has 200 services across 5 VPCs with complex inter-service communication patterns. Services need service discovery, circuit breaking, and observability. Which network architecture provides optimal service communication?
options: API Gateway with Lambda integrations
Application Load Balancer with service mesh
Service mesh with sidecar proxies
Direct service-to-service communication
explanation: Service mesh with sidecar proxies (like AWS App Mesh) provides service discovery, traffic management, circuit breaking, and observability for complex microservices communication patterns. API Gateway adds latency for internal communication. ALB alone lacks service mesh features. Direct communication lacks management capabilities.

text: A healthcare platform requires HIPAA-compliant network architecture with encrypted data in transit, network segmentation for PII data, and audit logging of all network traffic. Which combination ensures compliance and performance? (Select THREE)
options: VPC Flow Logs for network traffic audit
PrivateLink for service access
TLS encryption for all communications
Network Load Balancer for traffic distribution
Transit Gateway for network segmentation
CloudTrail for API logging
explanation: VPC Flow Logs provide comprehensive network traffic auditing for compliance. PrivateLink ensures private service access without internet routing. TLS encryption secures data in transit meeting HIPAA requirements. NLB provides performance but not compliance features. Transit Gateway aids segmentation but isn't compliance-specific. CloudTrail logs API calls, not network traffic.

text: A global application spans 6 AWS regions with requirements for disaster recovery, data residency compliance, and <50ms inter-region communication for critical operations. Each region hosts complete application stacks. Which network topology optimizes global performance and compliance?
options: Full mesh VPC peering between all regions
Hub-and-spoke with central region as hub
Regional clusters with Transit Gateway peering
Active-passive with primary and backup regions
explanation: Regional clusters with Transit Gateway peering provide optimal performance through regional traffic optimization while TGW peering enables controlled inter-region communication for DR scenarios. Full mesh creates excessive complexity. Hub-and-spoke adds unnecessary latency. Active-passive doesn't support <50ms requirement for all operations.

text: A financial company has 500TB of transaction data in S3 stored as CSV files with daily partitions. Business analysts need to run ad-hoc SQL queries with sub-second response times for regulatory reporting. The solution must be serverless and cost-optimized. Which architecture provides optimal query performance?
options: Athena with data converted to Parquet format and columnar compression
Redshift Serverless with CSV data loaded daily
EMR with Spark SQL and in-memory caching
QuickSight with direct S3 CSV connections
explanation: Athena with Parquet provides serverless, pay-per-query model with columnar format optimizing query performance and cost. Parquet compression reduces scan costs significantly. Redshift Serverless requires data loading overhead. EMR needs cluster management. QuickSight direct CSV connections are slow for large datasets.

text: A retail company needs real-time dashboards for 1000+ business users showing sales metrics from multiple data sources: RDS, DynamoDB, and S3 data lake. The solution must support row-level security and auto-scaling. Which combination provides optimal visualization architecture?
options: QuickSight with SPICE engine and dataset refresh
Grafana on ECS with ElastiCache for performance
Tableau Server on EC2 with dedicated instances
Custom React dashboard with API Gateway
explanation: QuickSight with SPICE provides auto-scaling visualization for 1000+ users, supports row-level security, connects to multiple AWS data sources natively, and offers pay-per-user pricing. Grafana lacks business intelligence features. Tableau requires infrastructure management. Custom dashboards require significant development effort.

text: A healthcare organization maintains a 10PB data lake with sensitive patient data. They need to implement fine-grained access controls, data lineage tracking, and automated data discovery across 50+ data sources. Which service combination provides comprehensive data governance?
options: Lake Formation with Glue Data Catalog and CloudTrail
S3 bucket policies with Athena workgroups
IAM roles with resource-based policies
Macie with Config for compliance monitoring
explanation: Lake Formation provides centralized data lake security with fine-grained permissions, Glue Data Catalog offers metadata management and data lineage, CloudTrail tracks access for audit. S3 policies alone lack fine-grained controls. IAM roles don't provide data discovery. Macie is for data classification, not governance.

text: A media company receives 50GB video files from content creators at unpredictable intervals (1-100 files daily). Files need immediate processing for transcoding and metadata extraction. The solution must handle burst traffic cost-effectively. Which ingestion pattern optimizes for variable workloads?
options: S3 Event Notifications triggering Lambda functions
CloudWatch Events with scheduled processing
SQS with EC2 Auto Scaling for processing
Direct upload to EMR with file monitoring
explanation: S3 Event Notifications with Lambda provide event-driven processing that scales automatically with file uploads, cost-effective for variable workloads. CloudWatch Events require scheduling, not event-driven. SQS with EC2 adds infrastructure overhead. EMR is expensive for intermittent processing.

text: A research institution needs to migrate 2PB of genomic data from on-premises NFS storage to S3, maintaining file permissions and metadata. The data center has 1Gbps internet connection, and migration must complete within 30 days. Which transfer solution meets the requirements?
options: DataSync with VPC endpoint over Direct Connect
S3 Transfer Acceleration with multipart upload
AWS Snowmobile with expedited shipping
Storage Gateway File Gateway with local caching
explanation: Snowmobile handles 2PB efficiently within 30 days (100PB capacity per truck), maintains file metadata, and is cost-effective for this data volume. DataSync over 1Gbps would take 185+ days. Transfer Acceleration doesn't maintain NFS permissions. File Gateway is for hybrid access, not migration.

text: A manufacturing company has 500 edge locations generating 100GB daily each. Data needs secure, automated transfer to S3 for analytics. Each location has unreliable internet connectivity. Which solution provides resilient data transfer?
options: DataSync agents with retry mechanisms and bandwidth throttling
S3 sync with CloudWatch monitoring
Storage Gateway Volume Gateway at each location
Snowball Edge devices with periodic pickup
explanation: DataSync agents provide automated, resilient transfers with built-in retry, bandwidth control, and network optimization for unreliable connections. S3 sync lacks advanced transfer optimization. Volume Gateway is for block storage. Snowball Edge requires physical logistics at scale.

text: A media company needs to transfer 50TB of video assets daily from multiple global offices to a centralized S3 data lake. Transfer must be encrypted, cost-optimized, and complete within 4-hour windows. Which combination optimizes global data transfer? (Select TWO)
options: S3 Transfer Acceleration for global uploads
DataSync with encryption in transit
Direct Connect at each office location
Snowball devices for daily transfers
CloudFront for upload optimization
Multipart upload with parallelization
explanation: S3 Transfer Acceleration optimizes global uploads using CloudFront edge locations. Multipart upload with parallelization maximizes throughput for large files within 4-hour windows. DataSync is for file systems. Direct Connect is expensive for multiple offices. Snowball isn't suitable for daily transfers.

text: A data lake contains 10TB of CSV files that need transformation to Parquet format with schema evolution support and incremental processing. The transformation runs nightly and must handle schema changes automatically. Which service provides optimal ETL capabilities?
options: AWS Glue with crawlers and dynamic frames
EMR with Spark and custom schemas
Lambda functions with pandas processing
Athena CREATE TABLE AS SELECT queries
explanation: AWS Glue with crawlers automatically discovers schema changes, dynamic frames handle schema evolution, and built-in format conversion optimizes CSV to Parquet transformation. EMR requires custom code for schema evolution. Lambda has execution time limits. Athena CTAS doesn't support incremental processing efficiently.

text: A healthcare organization needs to transform 1TB of patient records daily from multiple formats (HL7, DICOM, CSV) into FHIR format for interoperability. Data contains PII requiring encryption and audit trails. Which transformation solution meets compliance requirements?
options: Glue with encryption and CloudTrail logging
EMR with HIPAA-compliant cluster configuration
Lambda with KMS encryption and logging
Batch jobs with encrypted EBS volumes
explanation: AWS Glue provides managed ETL with built-in encryption, integrates with KMS for key management, CloudTrail for audit trails, and supports complex data format transformations. EMR requires more infrastructure management. Lambda has timeout limitations for 1TB processing. Batch adds operational complexity.

text: A social media platform processes 1 million events per second with requirements for real-time analytics, machine learning inference, and long-term storage. Different consumers need different processing latencies. Which streaming architecture provides optimal flexibility?
options: Kinesis Data Streams with multiple consumer applications
SQS FIFO with batch processing
MSK with multiple topic partitions
EventBridge with rule-based routing
explanation: Kinesis Data Streams supports multiple consumers with different processing patterns: enhanced fan-out for real-time ML, standard consumers for analytics, and Kinesis Firehose for S3 archival. SQS FIFO has throughput limits. MSK adds operational overhead. EventBridge is for event routing, not stream processing.

text: A gaming platform needs to process player events with exactly-once delivery guarantees and ordered processing per player. The system handles 100,000 players with burst patterns during events. Which streaming solution ensures data consistency?
options: Kinesis Data Streams with shard key per player
SQS FIFO with message group ID per player
MSK with idempotent producers
EventBridge with duplicate detection
explanation: MSK with idempotent producers provides exactly-once semantics with ordered processing per partition (player). Kafka's transaction support ensures data consistency. Kinesis doesn't guarantee exactly-once delivery. SQS FIFO has throughput limitations for 100,000 players. EventBridge lacks ordered processing guarantees.

text: A data lake stores sensitive customer data across multiple S3 buckets with different security classifications (public, internal, confidential, restricted). Access must be governed by user roles and data classification with audit logging. Which security architecture ensures proper access control?
options: Lake Formation with row and column-level security
S3 Access Control Lists with user-based permissions
IAM policies with resource-based conditions
Separate AWS accounts per classification level
explanation: Lake Formation provides table, column, and row-level security with centralized permission management, integrates with IAM for user roles, and maintains comprehensive audit logs. ACLs don't provide fine-grained controls. IAM alone lacks data-level permissions. Separate accounts add operational complexity.

text: A healthcare data lake contains patient records requiring encryption at rest and in transit, key rotation, and access logging for HIPAA compliance. The solution must support cross-region replication for disaster recovery. Which security implementation meets all requirements? (Select THREE)
options: S3 default encryption with AWS KMS customer-managed keys
CloudTrail with data events for S3 access logging
VPC endpoints for private S3 access
Cross-region replication with replication encryption
GuardDuty for threat detection
Config rules for compliance monitoring
explanation: KMS customer-managed keys with rotation meet HIPAA encryption requirements. CloudTrail data events provide comprehensive access logging for compliance. Cross-region replication with encryption maintains security during disaster recovery. VPC endpoints improve security but aren't required. GuardDuty and Config add value but aren't core requirements.

text: A financial firm processes time-series data requiring sub-second query responses for risk calculations. The workload needs 200GB of memory per node and processes 10TB datasets. Processing runs continuously during market hours (8 hours daily). Which configuration provides optimal performance?
options: EMR with memory-optimized instances and in-memory caching
Redshift with RA3 instances and result caching
ElastiCache Redis cluster with data preprocessing
EC2 with high-memory instances and custom applications
explanation: EMR with memory-optimized instances (like r5) provides the required 200GB+ memory per node, Spark in-memory caching optimizes iterative time-series processing, and managed service reduces operational overhead. Redshift is for data warehousing. ElastiCache lacks compute capabilities. EC2 requires custom implementation.

text: A media company processes video content requiring transcoding, thumbnail generation, and metadata extraction. Jobs vary from 1GB to 100GB files with unpredictable arrival patterns. The solution must minimize costs while handling burst capacity. Which compute strategy optimizes for variable workloads?
options: EMR with auto-scaling and mixed instance types
Batch with Fargate Spot for containerized processing
Lambda with increased timeout and memory limits
ECS with Auto Scaling and capacity providers
explanation: AWS Batch with Fargate Spot provides serverless compute that automatically scales for variable workloads, supports containers for media processing tools, and Spot pricing reduces costs up to 90%. EMR has minimum cluster overhead. Lambda has 15-minute timeout limits. ECS requires more capacity management.

text: A data lake contains 500TB of CSV files partitioned by date. Analytical queries scan large datasets causing high costs and slow performance. The solution must convert to an optimized format while preserving partition structure and enabling schema evolution. Which transformation approach provides optimal query performance and cost reduction?
options: Glue ETL jobs to convert CSV to Parquet with automatic partitioning
Athena CTAS queries to create Parquet tables from CSV
EMR Spark jobs with custom partition logic
Lambda functions with pandas for format conversion
explanation: Glue ETL provides managed transformation from CSV to Parquet with automatic schema discovery, partition preservation, and push-down predicate optimization. Parquet reduces storage costs by 80%+ and query times by 90%+. Athena CTAS doesn't handle schema evolution well. EMR requires custom development. Lambda has memory and timeout constraints.

text: A streaming application receives JSON data that needs real-time conversion to Avro format for downstream Kafka consumers. The transformation includes data validation, schema registry integration, and error handling. Which solution provides optimal streaming format conversion?
options: Kinesis Analytics with JSON to Avro transformation
Kinesis Firehose with data format conversion
MSK Connect with Schema Registry integration
Lambda functions triggered by Kinesis events
explanation: MSK Connect with Confluent Schema Registry provides native Kafka integration for JSON to Avro conversion with schema evolution, validation, and error handling. Kinesis Analytics lacks Avro support. Firehose doesn't support real-time Avro conversion. Lambda adds latency for streaming data.

text: A data warehouse migration project needs to transform 10TB of legacy fixed-width files to Delta Lake format with ACID transaction support. The transformation includes data quality checks, deduplication, and incremental updates. Which solution provides optimal batch transformation capabilities?
options: EMR with Delta Lake and Spark structured streaming
Glue with DynamicFrames and Delta Lake support
Databricks on AWS with optimized Delta Lake
Athena with CREATE TABLE AS SELECT for Delta format
explanation: Databricks provides optimized Delta Lake implementation with ACID transactions, advanced data quality features, and performance optimizations for large-scale transformations. EMR lacks Delta Lake optimizations. Glue doesn't fully support Delta Lake features. Athena cannot create Delta Lake tables directly.

text: A media company stores 500TB of video content with the following access patterns: 20% accessed within 30 days, 60% accessed 1-6 months after upload, and 20% archived for compliance (accessed once per year). They want to minimize storage costs while maintaining access performance. Which S3 storage strategy provides optimal cost optimization?
options: Store all data in S3 Standard with manual tier transitions
Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering for all objects with optional Archive Access tiers
Lifecycle policy: Standard → Standard-IA (30 days) → Glacier Flexible Retrieval (180 days)
Store hot data in Standard, warm data in One Zone-IA, cold data in Glacier Instant Retrieval
explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between access tiers based on changing access patterns without retrieval fees or performance impact. With Archive Access tiers enabled, it can move to Deep Archive for the 20% rarely accessed content, providing optimal cost savings for unpredictable access patterns. Manual policies require predicting access patterns and may misclassify data.

text: A startup hosts user-generated content with unpredictable access patterns. Some images go viral and are accessed millions of times, while others are rarely viewed. They need a cost-effective solution that automatically optimizes storage costs without manual intervention. Which approach minimizes both storage and request costs?
options: S3 Standard for all objects with CloudFront caching
S3 Intelligent-Tiering with CloudFront for frequently accessed content
Manual lifecycle policies based on CloudWatch metrics
S3 Standard-IA with lifecycle to Glacier after 30 days
explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically optimizes storage costs for unpredictable access patterns, while CloudFront reduces request costs for frequently accessed content by caching at edge locations. This combination handles viral content efficiently while minimizing costs for rarely accessed files. Standard alone is expensive for infrequently accessed content. Manual policies cannot predict viral patterns.

text: A database workload requires 20,000 IOPS with 99.9% uptime. The database size is 2TB and grows by 100GB monthly. Current setup uses io2 volumes with 20,000 provisioned IOPS. Which storage optimization reduces costs while maintaining performance requirements?
options: Switch to gp3 volumes with 20,000 IOPS provisioned
Use io2 Block Express for better price-performance
Implement automated EBS snapshots for cost optimization
Use gp3 with baseline performance and burst credits
explanation: gp3 volumes can provision up to 16,000 IOPS at lower cost than io2, and multiple gp3 volumes can achieve 20,000 total IOPS more cost-effectively. gp3 also provides consistent performance without burst limitations. io2 Block Express is more expensive and overkill for this requirement. Snapshots provide backup, not performance optimization. gp3 baseline (3,000 IOPS) is insufficient.

text: A data analytics workload processes large datasets sequentially during nightly batch jobs. The workload requires 2TB storage with high throughput but can tolerate moderate IOPS. The solution must be cost-optimized for this specific access pattern. Which EBS configuration provides optimal cost-performance?
options: gp3 volumes with maximum throughput provisioned
st1 (Throughput Optimized HDD) volumes
sc1 (Cold HDD) volumes for maximum cost savings
io2 volumes with provisioned IOPS for consistency
explanation: st1 (Throughput Optimized HDD) is designed for sequential access patterns with high throughput requirements at lower cost than SSD options. It provides up to 500 MB/s throughput per volume, ideal for batch processing workloads that don't require high IOPS. gp3 is more expensive for throughput-focused workloads. sc1 has lower throughput. io2 is expensive and unnecessary for sequential access.

text: A company requires 7-year retention of 500TB database backups for regulatory compliance. Backups are created daily but retrievals are rare (once per quarter for audits). The current solution stores all backups in S3 Standard. Which backup strategy minimizes long-term storage costs?
options: Lifecycle policy to move backups to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days
Use AWS Backup with Glacier Vault Lock for compliance
Implement cross-region replication to reduce costs
Store backups in S3 One Zone-IA for cost savings
explanation: S3 Glacier Deep Archive provides the lowest storage cost ($0.00099/GB-month) for long-term retention with rare access, reducing costs by 95% compared to S3 Standard. 30-day transition allows time for any immediate recovery needs while minimizing storage costs for the 7-year retention period. AWS Backup adds management overhead. Cross-region replication increases costs. One Zone-IA lacks the durability required for compliance.

text: A financial services company needs to backup 100TB of critical data with requirements: 15-minute RPO, 4-hour RTO, and 10-year retention. They want to optimize costs while meeting strict recovery requirements. Which backup architecture provides optimal cost-performance balance?
options: AWS Backup to S3 with immediate Glacier Deep Archive transition
EBS snapshots every 15 minutes with lifecycle management to Deep Archive
Continuous replication to another region with S3 Cross-Region Replication
AWS Backup with multiple storage tiers and automated lifecycle management
explanation: AWS Backup provides centralized backup management with automatic lifecycle transitions to optimize costs over the 10-year retention period. It can meet 15-minute RPO through incremental backups and provides restoration capabilities for 4-hour RTO. Automated tiering reduces long-term costs while maintaining recovery requirements. Immediate Deep Archive transition violates RTO. EBS snapshots alone lack centralized management. CRR is expensive for backup purposes.

text: An organization has 1PB of unstructured data backups stored across multiple S3 buckets with inconsistent lifecycle policies. They want to implement a unified backup strategy that automatically optimizes costs based on access patterns while maintaining compliance. Which solution provides comprehensive backup cost optimization? (Select TWO)
options: AWS Backup for centralized backup management
S3 Intelligent-Tiering for automatic cost optimization
S3 Storage Lens for usage analytics and optimization recommendations
AWS Config for backup compliance monitoring
Cross-region replication for disaster recovery
EBS snapshot lifecycle policies
explanation: AWS Backup provides centralized management for consistent backup policies across all services and storage types. S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically optimizes storage costs by moving data between access tiers based on access patterns without manual intervention. Storage Lens provides analytics but doesn't optimize costs automatically. Config monitors compliance but doesn't manage backups. CRR increases costs.

text: A manufacturing company has 50TB of CAD files on-premises that need migration to AWS. Files are accessed daily by engineers but historical versions (90% of data) are rarely accessed. They want to maintain on-premises performance while reducing storage costs. Which hybrid storage solution optimizes costs and performance?
options: AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway in cached mode
AWS DataSync with S3 Intelligent-Tiering
AWS Storage Gateway File Gateway with S3 lifecycle policies
Direct Connect with EFS for hybrid access
explanation: File Gateway provides NFS/SMB interface for on-premises access while storing data as S3 objects. S3 lifecycle policies automatically transition rarely accessed historical versions to cheaper storage tiers. This maintains performance for active files while optimizing costs for historical data. Volume Gateway is for block storage. DataSync is for migration, not ongoing hybrid access. Direct Connect with EFS is expensive for 50TB.

text: A global company has offices in 20 locations, each generating 1TB of data monthly that needs centralized backup to AWS. Each location has limited bandwidth (100Mbps) and requires local access to recent data. Which solution minimizes data transfer costs and provides local performance?
options: Deploy Storage Gateway File Gateway at each location
Use AWS DataSync agents with bandwidth throttling
Implement S3 Transfer Acceleration for faster uploads
Deploy EFS with regional mount targets
explanation: Storage Gateway File Gateway at each location provides local caching for frequently accessed data while automatically uploading to S3. This optimizes bandwidth usage by only transferring changed data and provides local performance. DataSync is better for one-time migrations. Transfer Acceleration improves speed but doesn't reduce data volume. EFS doesn't provide local caching benefits.

text: A research institution needs to migrate 500TB of genomic data from tape storage to AWS over 6 months. The data will be accessed infrequently (once per month per dataset). They want to minimize migration and long-term storage costs. Which approach provides optimal cost efficiency?
options: AWS Snowball Edge devices with direct Glacier upload
AWS DataSync over Direct Connect with S3 Standard-IA
Multiple Snowball devices with S3 Intelligent-Tiering
