AWS Transfer Family with S3 lifecycle policies
explanation: Multiple Snowball devices provide cost-effective offline transfer for 500TB, avoiding months of bandwidth costs. S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically optimizes storage costs for infrequently accessed data without retrieval fees or minimum storage duration charges. Snowball to Glacier requires additional processing costs. DataSync over Direct Connect is expensive for one-time migration. Transfer Family is for ongoing transfers.

text: A content creation company needs shared storage for 100 video editors accessing 200TB of active projects. Files are accessed randomly throughout the day with high throughput requirements. After project completion (3 months), files are rarely accessed but must remain available. Which storage solution optimizes costs and performance?
options: EFS with Intelligent-Tiering and lifecycle policies
FSx for Lustre with S3 integration for archival
EFS Standard with manual file management
FSx for Windows File Server with deduplication
explanation: EFS with Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves infrequently accessed files to lower-cost storage tiers while maintaining high throughput for active files. Lifecycle policies can transition completed projects to Infrequent Access storage. This provides the shared access needed by 100 editors while optimizing costs for aging data. FSx Lustre is expensive for general file sharing. Manual management is operationally complex.

text: A financial trading firm requires 10GB/s throughput for market data analysis during trading hours (8 hours daily) but minimal access during off-hours. They need 50TB capacity with submillisecond latency. Cost optimization is important due to limited usage hours. Which storage configuration provides optimal cost-performance for this usage pattern?
options: FSx for Lustre with persistent deployment and auto-scaling
EFS with Max I/O mode and provisioned throughput
FSx for Lustre scratch filesystem recreated daily
EBS with multiple io2 Block Express volumes in RAID
explanation: FSx for Lustre scratch filesystem provides the required 10GB/s+ throughput with submillisecond latency at lower cost than persistent storage. Recreating daily for 8-hour usage provides 70% cost savings compared to persistent deployment while meeting performance requirements. Persistent FSx wastes costs during 16 off-hours. EFS cannot achieve submillisecond latency. RAID volumes are complex and expensive.

text: A software development team needs shared storage for source code repositories, build artifacts, and documentation. 50 developers need concurrent access with version control. Current files (20TB) grow by 5TB monthly. Long-term retention is required but access decreases over time. Which solution balances collaboration needs with cost optimization?
options: EFS Standard with periodic cleanup of old files
EFS with Intelligent-Tiering for automatic cost optimization
S3 with static website hosting for documentation
FSx for Windows File Server with deduplication enabled
explanation: EFS with Intelligent-Tiering provides shared file access for 50 developers while automatically moving infrequently accessed files (old versions, archived projects) to lower-cost tiers. This balances collaborative needs with cost optimization as the repository grows. Manual cleanup risks losing important historical data. S3 doesn't provide the shared file system semantics needed for development workflows.

text: You must restrict an Amazon API Gateway endpoint so only a partner VPC via VPC endpoint can invoke it. Which control is appropriate?
options: IAM identity policy on the partner account
API Gateway resource policy allowing only the VPC endpoint principal
Lambda function resource policy
NACL rules on the API Gateway subnet
explanation: Use an API Gateway resource policy to allow only requests from the specified VPC endpoint.

text: A company operates 500 S3 buckets across multiple AWS accounts with inconsistent storage class usage and lifecycle policies. They want to identify cost optimization opportunities and implement automated cost controls. Which combination provides comprehensive storage cost management? (Select TWO)
options: S3 Storage Lens for usage analytics and cost insights
AWS Cost Explorer with storage-specific cost allocation tags
S3 Intelligent-Tiering enabled on all buckets
AWS Budgets with S3 storage cost alerts
AWS Config rules for lifecycle policy compliance
S3 Inventory for object-level cost analysis
explanation: S3 Storage Lens provides comprehensive storage analytics across all accounts with cost optimization recommendations and usage trends. Cost Explorer with cost allocation tags enables detailed analysis of storage costs by department, project, or application, identifying optimization opportunities. While other options provide value, these two give the most comprehensive cost management capabilities.

text: A media company's storage costs have increased 300% over 6 months due to rapid content growth. They need to implement cost controls and optimization strategies across their 10TB daily uploads to S3. Which approach provides immediate and long-term cost reduction?
options: Implement S3 request metrics and optimize upload patterns
Enable S3 Intelligent-Tiering with Archive Access tiers
Set up AWS Budgets with automatic cost control actions
Use S3 Storage Lens to identify cost optimization opportunities
explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering with Archive Access tiers automatically optimizes storage costs for the growing content library by moving data to the most cost-effective tier based on access patterns. With rapid growth, this provides immediate cost benefits and scales automatically. Request metrics help but don't address storage class optimization. Budgets provide alerts but don't optimize existing storage. Storage Lens provides insights but requires manual action.

text: An organization wants to implement Requester Pays on their S3 bucket containing 50TB of research data accessed by external collaborators. Some collaborators access data frequently while others access it rarely. Which configuration optimizes costs for all parties?
options: Enable Requester Pays on the entire bucket
Use S3 Access Points with different billing configurations
Create separate buckets for frequent and infrequent users
Implement S3 Intelligent-Tiering with Requester Pays
explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering with Requester Pays optimizes storage costs by automatically moving data to appropriate tiers while transferring data transfer and request costs to requesters. This benefits frequent users through lower storage costs and occasional users pay only for what they access. Simple Requester Pays doesn't optimize storage costs. Access Points add complexity. Separate buckets require data duplication.

text: A global application serves 100TB of static content monthly from S3 to users worldwide. Current data transfer costs are $9,000/month. They need to reduce these costs while maintaining performance for global users. Which solution provides maximum cost reduction?
options: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration for faster downloads
Implement CloudFront distribution with origin in lowest-cost region
Use S3 Cross-Region Replication to serve users from nearest region
Compress all content before storing in S3
explanation: CloudFront distribution can reduce data transfer costs by 50-80% by serving content from edge locations instead of S3 directly. CloudFront data transfer rates are lower than S3 internet transfer rates, and caching reduces origin requests. Transfer Acceleration improves speed but doesn't reduce costs. CRR increases storage costs. Compression helps but the savings are limited compared to CloudFront.

text: A SaaS company replicates user data across 3 AWS regions for disaster recovery. The current approach uses S3 Cross-Region Replication for all 200TB of data, costing $2,000 monthly in replication charges. Which optimization reduces replication costs while maintaining recovery capabilities? (Select TWO)
options: Implement selective replication based on data criticality
Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering in destination regions
Enable S3 Replication Time Control for faster replication
Use lifecycle policies to replicate only to Standard-IA
Implement backup-based disaster recovery instead of replication
Compress data before replication to reduce transfer volume
explanation: Selective replication based on data criticality can reduce replication volume by 50-80% by only replicating essential data for disaster recovery. Backup-based disaster recovery using AWS Backup can be more cost-effective than real-time replication for non-critical workloads. Intelligent-Tiering doesn't reduce replication costs. RTC increases costs. Lifecycle policies don't apply to replicated data. Compression helps but has limited impact.

text: A video streaming platform stores 2PB of content across multiple S3 storage classes. Analysis shows: 5% accessed daily (hot), 15% accessed weekly (warm), 30% accessed monthly (cool), and 50% accessed rarely (cold). Current storage costs are $40,000 monthly. Which optimization strategy provides maximum cost reduction?
options: Migrate all data to S3 One Zone-IA for cost savings
Implement granular lifecycle policies based on access patterns
Enable S3 Intelligent-Tiering on all objects with all access tiers
Use S3 Storage Lens analytics to optimize storage classes manually
explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering with all access tiers (including Archive Instant Access and Deep Archive Access) automatically optimizes storage costs based on actual access patterns without retrieval fees or performance impact. For 2PB with varied access patterns, this can reduce costs by 40-70%. Manual lifecycle policies require predicting patterns and risk misclassification. One Zone-IA doesn't optimize for different access frequencies. Storage Lens provides insights but requires manual optimization.

text: A data analytics company processes datasets that follow a predictable pattern: intensive compute access for 1 week, occasional analysis for 3 months, then archive storage for compliance. They want to optimize storage costs across the entire data lifecycle automatically. Which solution provides hands-off cost optimization?
options: S3 Intelligent-Tiering with optional Archive tiers
Manual lifecycle policy: Standard → Standard-IA → Glacier
EFS Intelligent-Tiering with lifecycle management
S3 with Lambda-based lifecycle automation
explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering with optional Archive Access tiers provides automatic cost optimization throughout the entire lifecycle without manual intervention. It handles the intensive compute phase in Frequent Access, moves to Infrequent Access during occasional analysis, and automatically transitions to Archive tiers for compliance storage. Manual policies risk misclassifying data during variable access patterns. EFS is expensive for long-term archival. Lambda automation adds complexity.

text: A company needs to transfer 1PB of historical data from on-premises to S3 Glacier Deep Archive. They have a 1Gbps internet connection and want to minimize both transfer time and costs. The data will be accessed less than once per year. Which transfer method provides optimal cost and time efficiency?
options: AWS DataSync over existing internet connection
AWS Snowmobile for 1PB transfer
Multiple AWS Snowball Edge devices
AWS Direct Connect with data transfer
explanation: AWS Snowmobile is specifically designed for exabyte-scale transfers and provides the most cost-effective solution for 1PB. Transfer time is ~10 days vs 100+ days over 1Gbps internet. While Snowmobile has a higher base cost, it eliminates months of bandwidth costs and reduces transfer time significantly. Multiple Snowballs would require complex coordination. DataSync over internet takes too long. Direct Connect has high bandwidth costs for one-time transfer.

text: A multi-tenant SaaS platform serves 10,000 customers with 500TB total storage. Customer usage patterns vary dramatically: 20% power users consume 80% of storage and bandwidth, 60% normal users have predictable patterns, 20% trial users have minimal usage. Which cost optimization strategy maximizes efficiency across all customer segments? (Select THREE)
options: Implement S3 Intelligent-Tiering for automatic optimization across all customer data
Use cost allocation tags to track and optimize storage costs per customer tier
Enable S3 Requester Pays for power users to offset high bandwidth costs
Implement different storage classes based on customer tier (trial, normal, power)
Use S3 Storage Lens to analyze usage patterns and optimize storage classes
Set up AWS Budgets with alerts for unusual storage cost increases
explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically optimizes storage costs across all customer segments regardless of usage patterns. Cost allocation tags enable tracking and optimization per customer tier, allowing for different pricing models. S3 Storage Lens provides insights to optimize storage classes and identify cost anomalies across the multi-tenant environment. Requester Pays may not be suitable for SaaS model. Manual storage classes based on tiers are inflexible.

text: A data processing company runs batch jobs that require 500 EC2 instances for 4 hours daily during off-peak hours. Jobs can be interrupted and restarted without data loss. Current costs using On-Demand instances are $15,000 monthly. Which purchasing strategy provides maximum cost savings?
options: Purchase 500 Reserved Instances with 1-year term
Use Spot Fleet with diversified instance types across multiple AZs
Implement Compute Savings Plans for consistent hourly usage
Use Dedicated Hosts with Savings Plans for licensing benefits
explanation: Spot Fleet with diversification can provide 50-90% cost savings ($1,500-$7,500/month) compared to On-Demand for interruptible batch workloads. Diversifying across instance types and AZs reduces interruption risk. Reserved Instances require paying for 24/7 capacity when only 4 hours are needed. Savings Plans still pay for idle hours. Dedicated Hosts are expensive and unnecessary for this workload.

text: A memory-intensive application currently runs on 10 r5.4xlarge instances (16 vCPUs, 128GB RAM each) with average CPU utilization of 25% and memory utilization of 95%. The application is not CPU-bound. Which rightsizing strategy optimizes costs while maintaining performance?
options: Switch to 5 r5.8xlarge instances for better resource utilization
Migrate to 15 r5.2xlarge instances to match CPU usage
Use r6g.4xlarge instances with Graviton2 processors for cost savings
Deploy 10 x1e.2xlarge instances optimized for memory-intensive workloads
explanation: x1e.2xlarge instances provide 244GB RAM (double the memory) with 8 vCPUs for memory-intensive workloads at similar cost to r5.4xlarge. This better matches the high memory, low CPU usage pattern. Since memory is the constraint at 95% utilization, more memory per instance reduces instance count and costs. r5.8xlarge doesn't help with the memory constraint. More r5.2xlarge instances increase costs. r6g helps but doesn't address the fundamental memory requirement.

text: A web application runs on 50 t3.large instances with average CPU utilization of 15% during normal hours and brief spikes to 80% during traffic bursts. The application is cost-sensitive and can tolerate occasional performance delays. Which optimization provides maximum cost savings?
options: Migrate to t3.medium instances and scale horizontally
Enable T3 Unlimited mode for consistent performance
Switch to t4g.large instances with Graviton2 processors
Use c5.large instances for consistent CPU performance
explanation: t4g.large instances with Graviton2 processors provide up to 40% better price-performance than t3.large for web workloads while maintaining burstable performance characteristics. The low average CPU utilization (15%) fits perfectly with burstable instances. t3.medium might be too small for peak loads. T3 Unlimited incurs extra charges during bursts. c5.large instances are overkill and more expensive for this usage pattern.

text: A microservices API processes 1 million requests daily with average execution time of 200ms per request. Traffic is distributed evenly over 12 hours daily with zero traffic overnight. Current setup uses 5 t3.small instances running 24/7. Which architecture provides optimal cost efficiency?
options: Lambda functions for all API endpoints
Fargate containers with auto-scaling to zero
ECS with EC2 instances and scheduled scaling
API Gateway with Lambda for compute-intensive operations only
explanation: Lambda functions eliminate idle time costs (12 hours daily) and provide automatic scaling. Cost calculation: 1M requests × 200ms × $0.0000166667/GB-second + $0.20/1M requests ≈ $0.55/day vs t3.small instances at ~$15/day. Lambda's pay-per-use model is ideal for predictable request patterns with zero overnight usage. Fargate still has minimum task costs. ECS with EC2 pays for idle capacity. API Gateway adds unnecessary complexity.

text: A batch processing application runs monthly reports that take 6 hours to complete using 20 EC2 instances. The application runs once per month but instances currently run 24/7. Processing cannot be interrupted once started. Which solution optimizes costs for this workload?
options: AWS Batch with EC2 Spot instances
Lambda functions with 15-minute timeout
ECS tasks on Fargate with reserved capacity
Scheduled EC2 instances with On-Demand pricing
explanation: AWS Batch with EC2 Spot instances provides up to 90% cost savings for batch workloads. Batch handles spot interruptions with job queues and retries, ensuring completion despite interruptions. Monthly usage (6 hours vs 744 hours) makes spot interruption risk acceptable. Lambda has 15-minute timeout limits. Fargate reserved capacity still charges for unused time. Scheduled On-Demand is expensive compared to Spot pricing.

text: A web application experiences predictable daily traffic patterns: 10 instances needed from 6 AM-10 PM, 3 instances overnight. Current setup maintains 10 instances 24/7. Which auto-scaling strategy optimizes costs while ensuring availability?
options: Target tracking scaling based on CPU utilization
Scheduled scaling with time-based policies
Step scaling with aggressive scale-down policies
Predictive scaling using machine learning
explanation: Scheduled scaling with time-based policies perfectly matches predictable traffic patterns, providing immediate cost savings of ~42% (10 instances → 3 instances for 8 hours daily). Predictable patterns don't benefit from reactive scaling delays. Target tracking and step scaling add lag time and may not reach optimal capacity quickly. Predictive scaling adds complexity for simple predictable patterns and has additional costs.

text: A microservices architecture serves web traffic through a load balancer to 20 different service endpoints. Traffic patterns vary significantly between services. Current setup uses an Application Load Balancer with target groups. Which optimization reduces load balancer costs?
options: Use Network Load Balancer for lower per-hour costs
Implement multiple ALBs per service for better distribution
Use Gateway Load Balancer for advanced routing
Consolidate low-traffic services behind a single ALB with path-based routing
explanation: Consolidating low-traffic services behind a single ALB with path-based routing reduces the number of load balancers needed while maintaining functionality. ALB supports 100 rules per listener, enabling efficient consolidation. Each ALB costs ~$22/month, so reducing from multiple ALBs to fewer ALBs provides direct cost savings. Network Load Balancer doesn't support HTTP routing. Multiple ALBs increase costs. Gateway Load Balancer is for network appliances.

text: A platform role has broad S3 permissions. You want to further limit access per session when assumed by a CI job. What mechanism should you use?
options: Add an inline policy to the role
Attach an SCP to the account
Pass a session policy with AssumeRole to scope permissions
Use a bucket policy to deny the role
explanation: Session policies scope down the effective permissions of the role during that session only.

text: A gaming application requires extremely low latency for UDP traffic across multiple regions. Current setup uses Application Load Balancers in each region. The application needs to optimize both performance and costs. Which load balancing strategy provides the best cost-performance ratio?
options: Upgrade to Network Load Balancers for UDP support and lower latency
Implement Global Accelerator with regional Network Load Balancers
Use Route 53 latency-based routing without load balancers
Deploy Gateway Load Balancers for advanced traffic management
explanation: Global Accelerator with regional NLBs provides optimal UDP performance using AWS global network while reducing the number of NLBs needed (consolidated endpoints). Global Accelerator costs $18/month per accelerator plus data transfer, but reduces regional NLB costs and improves performance significantly. Simple NLB upgrade doesn't optimize cross-region performance. Route 53 alone lacks load balancing capabilities. Gateway Load Balancer is for network appliances.

text: A containerized application runs 50 microservices with varying resource requirements. Current ECS setup uses c5.large instances with 50% average cluster utilization. Each service has unpredictable scaling patterns. Which container strategy optimizes resource utilization and costs?
options: Migrate to Fargate for automatic resource allocation per task
Use ECS with Spot instances and cluster auto-scaling
Implement EKS with mixed instance types and node auto-scaling
Use ECS with Capacity Providers mixing On-Demand and Spot instances
explanation: ECS with Capacity Providers mixing On-Demand and Spot instances provides optimal cost optimization. On-Demand instances ensure baseline availability while Spot instances (60-90% savings) handle variable loads. Capacity Providers automatically balance cost and availability. Fargate eliminates unused capacity but has higher per-vCPU costs. Pure Spot risks availability. EKS adds operational complexity and costs.

text: A data processing pipeline runs containerized jobs that scale from 10 to 1000 containers based on queue depth. Jobs run for 2-30 minutes with varying memory requirements (512MB to 8GB). Current setup over-provisions resources. Which solution optimizes costs for variable container workloads?
options: ECS on EC2 with multiple instance types and auto-scaling
AWS Batch with Fargate for automatic resource allocation
Fargate with Application Auto Scaling based on queue metrics
EKS with Horizontal Pod Autoscaler and vertical pod autoscaling
explanation: AWS Batch with Fargate automatically allocates exact resources needed per job (512MB-8GB) without over-provisioning, scaling from 0 to 1000 containers seamlessly. Batch optimizes job scheduling and resource allocation. Pay only for resources used during job execution. ECS requires capacity planning. Plain Fargate lacks job queue management. EKS adds Kubernetes complexity and costs.

text: A CI/CD pipeline builds and tests applications using containerized build agents. Builds occur sporadically (50 builds daily) with peak periods requiring 20 concurrent builds. Current setup maintains 20 EC2 instances continuously. Which approach minimizes costs for bursty CI/CD workloads?
options: Use CodeBuild with on-demand compute environments
Implement ECS with Spot instances for build agents
Use self-hosted runners on EC2 with auto-scaling
Deploy GitLab runners on Fargate with auto-scaling
explanation: CodeBuild provides serverless CI/CD compute that charges only during build execution, eliminating idle time costs. For sporadic usage (50 builds vs 480 potential daily builds with 20 instances), this provides ~90% cost savings. No infrastructure management required. ECS with Spot still pays for idle capacity. Self-hosted runners require management overhead. Fargate runners still incur costs during idle periods.

text: A manufacturing company operates 100 factory locations requiring local data processing with cloud connectivity. Each location processes 10GB daily but peaks at 100GB during equipment maintenance. Current solution deploys EC2 instances at each location. Which edge computing approach reduces costs?
options: AWS IoT Greengrass with Lambda functions at edge locations
AWS Outposts with ECS containers for local processing
AWS Snowball Edge with compute instances
Local EC2 instances with AWS Systems Manager for management
explanation: IoT Greengrass with Lambda functions provides edge compute that scales automatically with workload (10GB normal, 100GB peaks) without maintaining always-on instances. Lambda pricing model is ideal for variable edge workloads. Greengrass synchronizes with cloud when connectivity is available. Outposts requires significant upfront investment and ongoing costs. Snowball Edge is for temporary deployments. Local EC2 instances still require 24/7 costs.

text: A content delivery platform needs compute power near users for real-time video transcoding. Current setup uses regional EC2 instances with low utilization outside peak hours. Video processing is CPU-intensive and latency-sensitive. Which strategy balances performance requirements with cost optimization? (Select TWO)
options: Lambda@Edge for lightweight transcoding operations
EC2 instances in Local Zones for ultra-low latency
CloudFront with origin processing using Auto Scaling
Wavelength zones with container-based transcoding
Regional Fargate tasks with Application Load Balancer routing
ECS clusters with Spot instances and predictive scaling
explanation: Wavelength zones provide ultra-low latency compute near users for real-time video transcoding with 5G network integration. ECS clusters with Spot instances (60-90% savings) and predictive scaling optimize costs during variable demand while maintaining performance. Lambda@Edge has execution time limits. Local Zones don't exist in all markets. CloudFront doesn't provide compute. Regional Fargate lacks proximity benefits.

text: A media company transcodes video content using FPGA-accelerated instances for specialized algorithms. Processing happens in batches: 10 hours weekly for regular content, 50 hours monthly for premium content. Current F1 instances run continuously. Which solution optimizes costs for FPGA workloads?
options: AWS Batch with F1 instances on Spot pricing
Reserved F1 instances for predictable capacity
EC2 Fleet with mixed F1 instance types
Custom AMI with automatic FPGA configuration
explanation: AWS Batch with F1 instances on Spot pricing provides job-based scheduling eliminating idle time costs (~92% time savings: 50 hours vs 744 hours monthly) plus 50-70% Spot discounts. Batch handles job queuing and spot interruptions with retries. F1 instances are expensive to run continuously. Reserved instances still pay for idle time. EC2 Fleet requires manual job management. Custom AMI doesn't address the scheduling optimization.

text: A company operates 500 EC2 instances across multiple projects with inconsistent tagging and cost allocation. They want to implement comprehensive cost tracking and optimization. Which combination provides effective compute cost management? (Select TWO)
options: AWS Cost Explorer with cost allocation tags for project tracking
EC2 Instance Scheduler for automated start/stop based on usage
AWS Budgets with alerts for cost anomalies and overruns
Trusted Advisor for rightsizing recommendations and unused resources
CloudWatch detailed monitoring for performance optimization
AWS Config for compliance tracking and cost governance
explanation: Cost Explorer with cost allocation tags enables detailed project-level cost analysis and trend identification for 500 instances. Trusted Advisor provides automated rightsizing recommendations and identifies unused resources, directly reducing compute costs. Budgets provide alerts but don't optimize costs. Instance Scheduler helps but only for predictable schedules. CloudWatch helps performance but not direct cost optimization.

text: A multi-account organization wants to optimize compute costs across 20 AWS accounts with different teams and projects. Each account has varying usage patterns and cost optimization maturity. Which centralized approach provides organization-wide compute cost optimization?
options: AWS Organizations with consolidated billing and shared Reserved Instances
Compute Optimizer recommendations across all linked accounts
AWS Cost and Usage Reports (CUR) with centralized analysis
All of the above implemented together for comprehensive optimization
explanation: Comprehensive optimization requires all components: Organizations with consolidated billing enables shared Reserved Instance benefits across accounts; Compute Optimizer provides rightsizing recommendations for all accounts; CUR enables detailed analysis and custom optimization strategies. Individual solutions provide partial benefits, but combined implementation addresses organization-wide cost optimization holistically with maximum impact.

text: A team granted themselves kms:Decrypt via IAM but still can't decrypt data. What is MOST likely missing?
options: A resource-based policy on KMS key allowing their principal
An SCP allowing kms:Decrypt
Enabling automatic key rotation
Grant tokens via AWS STS
explanation: KMS keys are governed primarily by the key policy; IAM permissions alone are insufficient if the key policy doesn't trust the principal.

text: A SaaS platform serves 10,000 customers with individual compute environments. Resource usage varies dramatically: 20% heavy users (80% of compute costs), 60% moderate users (15% of costs), 20% light users (5% of costs). Which cost optimization strategy maximizes efficiency across customer segments? (Select THREE)
options: Implement different instance families based on customer tier usage patterns
Use Spot instances for development and testing environments of all customers
Apply Savings Plans based on baseline usage patterns across all customer tiers
Enable detailed cost allocation tags to track and optimize per-customer costs
Use Lambda for light users and containers for moderate/heavy users
Implement auto-scaling policies tailored to each customer segment's usage patterns
explanation: Savings Plans based on baseline usage across all tiers provides foundational cost savings (~20-70% for committed usage). Detailed cost allocation tags enable per-customer cost tracking and optimization strategies. Tailored auto-scaling policies optimize each segment: aggressive scaling for light users, predictive scaling for heavy users. Instance families per tier add complexity. Spot instances risk customer experience. Lambda may not suit all light user workloads.

text: A company is moving to a multi-account strategy. Developers need console and CLI access to multiple accounts without long-lived access keys. Which approach best follows security best practices?
options: Create IAM users in each account and share access keys via a password manager
Create a single IAM user in the management account and share its access keys to all developers
Use IAM Identity Center (AWS SSO) with permission sets to grant roles in target accounts, providing short-lived credentials
Create cross-account access by attaching inline policies to the root user
explanation: Use IAM Identity Center to broker short-lived role sessions into target accounts; avoids long-lived keys and centralizes access.

text: An application in Account A must read objects from an S3 bucket in Account B without using static credentials. What's the most secure, scalable design?
options: Attach an S3 bucket policy in Account B that allows the IAM role from Account A to s3:GetObject
Create an IAM user in Account B with access keys and store them in Secrets Manager in Account A
Whitelist Account A's VPC CIDR in the S3 bucket policy
Enable S3 ACLs on objects and set public-read
explanation: Use a resource-based policy (S3 bucket policy) to trust the role principal from Account A; no long-lived keys needed.

text: In AWS Organizations, security wants to ensure no account can create Internet Gateways. Where should this be enforced?
options: Attach a deny statement to all IAM roles
Use a Service Control Policy (SCP) at the OU with a Deny on ec2:CreateInternetGateway
Create a Config rule in each account
Add a VPC endpoint policy for EC2 preventing creation
explanation: SCPs set the maximum available permissions across accounts; explicit Deny prevents the action regardless of local IAM.

text: Your private workloads access S3 via an endpoint. You need to restrict accessible buckets. Where do you enforce this?
options: IAM role inline policies only
S3 bucket ACLs only
VPC endpoint policy scoping to specific bucket ARNs (plus S3 bucket policies as needed)
Security group on the endpoint network interface
explanation: Combine VPC endpoint policy with S3 bucket policies to restrict which resources are reachable via the endpoint.

text: Which features help detect or prevent unintended public or cross-account access? (Select TWO)
options: IAM Access Analyzer
AWS Budgets
AWS Shield Advanced
S3 Block Public Access
CloudFront Signed URLs
explanation: Access Analyzer finds resource sharing risks; S3 Block Public Access prevents public S3 exposure.

text: A Lambda function must be invoked by API Gateway and also read from an S3 bucket. Which combination is correct?
options: Attach S3 permissions to the function's resource policy; allow API Gateway via IAM identity policy
Grant S3 access in the Lambda execution role; add a Lambda resource policy permission for apigateway.amazonaws.com
Use only resource policies for both S3 and Lambda
Use only the execution role; no resource policies are needed
explanation: Execution role for the function's actions (S3). Resource policy (lambda:InvokeFunction permission) to allow API Gateway to invoke.

text: Company-wide S3 Block Public Access is enabled. One static website bucket needs public READ only. What is the safest approach?
options: Disable Block Public Access on the account
Disable Block Public Access only on that bucket and use bucket policy granting s3:GetObject for public, no ACLs
Enable public ACLs and rely on ACLs only
Attach full s3:* to Everyone
explanation: Scope the exception to the specific bucket and grant minimal public read via bucket policy; keep account-level blocks elsewhere.

text: Why choose IAM Identity Center (AWS SSO) for workforce access across accounts? (Select TWO)
options: Short-lived credentials via role sessions
Central permission sets mapped to account roles
Generates long-lived access keys per user
Eliminates the need for MFA
Replaces SCPs
explanation: Identity Center manages role-based, short-lived access centrally; it doesn't create long-lived keys or replace SCPs/MFA.

text: Security team in a central account needs read-only access to all member accounts' CloudTrail logs in S3. What is the cleanest pattern?
options: Replicate all logs into the security account's bucket and allow access via bucket policy
Create IAM users in each account and share keys
Attach inline identity policies in member accounts trusting security account
Use SCPs to allow s3:GetObject only for security account
explanation: Centralize logs to a security-owned S3 bucket and grant access via bucket policy; avoids per-account users/keys.

text: In Amazon EKS, pods need AWS API access without node-wide credentials exposure. What should you implement?
options: Instance profile on worker nodes
Kube secrets with access keys
IAM Roles for Service Accounts (IRSA) with OIDC provider
S3 pre-signed URLs for all calls
explanation: IRSA maps Kubernetes service accounts to IAM roles via an OIDC provider, providing least-privilege short-lived creds per pod.

text: For which services are resource-based policies commonly used to grant cross-account access? (Select THREE)
options: S3
KMS keys
EC2 instances
Lambda
IAM users
explanation: S3 bucket policies, KMS key policies, and Lambda resource policies are standard resource-based policy patterns.

text: An auditor role needs access for only a few hours at a time. What STS configuration aligns with least privilege?
options: Increase MaxSessionDuration to 12 hours and share the credentials
Set a low MaxSessionDuration and require re-assumption; grant read-only policies
Create an IAM user for the auditor with access keys
Use root user access during audits
explanation: Short session durations with read-only permissions minimize exposure and align with least privilege.

text: Which statements about SCPs are correct? (Select TWO)
options: SCPs apply to all principals including root in member accounts
An explicit Deny in an SCP overrides an Allow in an identity policy
SCPs grant permissions directly
SCPs affect service-linked roles but not resource policies
SCPs are evaluated after resource policies
explanation: SCPs are permission guardrails (no grants) and their explicit Deny overrides allows. They apply to all principals, including root.

text: You created a role in Account B to be assumed by a role in Account A, but AssumeRole fails with access denied. Which file likely needs correction?
options: Account A role inline policy
The role trust policy in Account B
SCP in the management account
CloudTrail data event selector
explanation: Cross-account assumption requires the target role's trust policy to allow the principal from Account A.

text: A backend service generates pre-signed S3 URLs for client downloads. Which statement is TRUE?
options: Clients need IAM users to use pre-signed URLs
Bucket must be public
Access is authorized by the signature created with the signer's credentials and expires after a set time
Requires CloudFront signed cookies
explanation: Pre-signed URLs embed a signature derived from the signer's permissions and expire; clients need no IAM identity.

text: You store database credentials in Secrets Manager. Which controls help ensure only a specific Lambda function can read them? (Select TWO)
options: Grant secretsmanager:GetSecretValue in the Lambda execution role scoped to the secret ARN
Add a resource policy on the secret allowing only the Lambda execution role principal
Store the password in Lambda env vars and encrypt with KMS
Attach AdministratorAccess to the Lambda role for reliability
explanation: Combine execution-role identity policy with a resource policy on the secret to trust only that role.

text: A solutions architect is designing a three-tier web application on AWS. The application requires a web tier in public subnets, an application tier that should not be directly accessible from the internet, and a database tier with the highest level of network isolation. Which network architecture provides the MOST secure design while maintaining necessary connectivity?
options: Place all three tiers in public subnets and use security groups to control access between tiers
Place the web tier in public subnets, application and database tiers in the same private subnet, and use a NAT gateway for outbound internet access
Place the web tier in public subnets, application tier in private subnets with NAT gateway access, and database tier in isolated private subnets with no NAT gateway
Place all tiers in private subnets and use an Application Load Balancer with AWS WAF in public subnets
explanation: Option C provides defense in depth through proper network segmentation. The web tier in public subnets can receive internet traffic, the application tier in private subnets with NAT gateway can make outbound connections for updates while remaining inaccessible from the internet, and the database tier in isolated subnets without NAT gateway has maximum isolation with access only from the application tier. This follows AWS best practices for multi-tier architecture security.

text: A company needs to secure API credentials used by Lambda functions to access third-party services. The credentials must be encrypted at rest, automatically rotated every 30 days, and accessible only by specific Lambda functions. Which combination of AWS services provides the MOST secure solution?
options: Store credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store with SecureString type and use Lambda environment variables for access
Store credentials in AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation enabled and grant Lambda execution roles permissions to retrieve the secret
Store credentials in an S3 bucket with SSE-KMS encryption and use Lambda layers to distribute credentials
Store credentials in Amazon DynamoDB with encryption at rest and implement custom rotation logic in Lambda
explanation: AWS Secrets Manager is specifically designed for this use case. It provides automatic rotation capabilities for credentials, encryption at rest using KMS, and fine-grained access control through IAM policies. Lambda execution roles can be granted permissions to retrieve specific secrets, ensuring only authorized functions can access the credentials. This is more secure than Parameter Store (no automatic rotation), S3 (not designed for secrets), or DynamoDB (requires custom rotation logic).

text: A company is building a web application that requires user authentication with social media providers and needs to manage user profiles and preferences. The solution must support millions of users and provide token-based authentication for API access. Which AWS service best meets these requirements?
options: AWS IAM Identity Center with external identity provider integration
Amazon Cognito with User Pools and Identity Pools
AWS Directory Service with Active Directory federation
AWS SSO with SAML 2.0 federation
explanation: Amazon Cognito is designed specifically for application user authentication. User Pools handle user registration, authentication, and account recovery with support for social identity providers. Identity Pools provide temporary AWS credentials for API access. It scales to millions of users and provides JWT tokens for authentication. IAM Identity Center and SSO are for workforce identity, not application users. Directory Service is for enterprise directory integration.

text: A financial services company stores sensitive customer data in S3 buckets. They need to automatically discover, classify, and protect personally identifiable information (PII) across their S3 environment. Which AWS service should they implement?
options: Amazon GuardDuty with S3 protection enabled
Amazon Macie for sensitive data discovery and classification
AWS Config with custom rules for PII detection
Amazon Inspector for S3 bucket vulnerability scanning
explanation: Amazon Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to automatically discover, classify, and protect sensitive data in S3. It can identify PII, financial data, and other sensitive information types. GuardDuty focuses on threat detection, not data classification. Config tracks configuration changes but does not classify data. Inspector assesses EC2 instances and containers, not S3 data.

text: A company web application is experiencing SQL injection attempts and cross-site scripting attacks. The application runs behind an Application Load Balancer. Which solution provides the MOST comprehensive protection against these threats?
options: Enable AWS Shield Standard on the Application Load Balancer
Configure AWS WAF with managed rule sets for SQL injection and XSS protection
Implement Amazon GuardDuty to detect and block malicious requests
Use security groups to filter malicious traffic patterns
explanation: AWS WAF is specifically designed to protect web applications from common attacks like SQL injection and XSS. Managed rule sets provide pre-configured protections against these threats. WAF integrates with ALB to inspect and filter HTTP/HTTPS requests. Shield protects against DDoS, not application-layer attacks. GuardDuty detects threats but does not block traffic. Security groups operate at Layer 4 and can not inspect application-layer payloads.

text: An e-commerce application is experiencing a DDoS attack causing service degradation. The company needs immediate protection with access to AWS DDoS experts and cost protection for scaling resources. Which solution should they implement?
options: Enable AWS Shield Standard and configure Auto Scaling
Upgrade to AWS Shield Advanced with DDoS Response Team support
Implement AWS WAF with rate-limiting rules
Deploy Amazon CloudFront with AWS Shield Standard
explanation: AWS Shield Advanced provides enhanced DDoS protection with 24/7 access to the DDoS Response Team (DRT), advanced attack diagnostics, and cost protection against DDoS-related scaling charges. Shield Standard provides basic protection but lacks DRT support and cost protection. WAF helps with application-layer attacks but is not comprehensive DDoS protection. CloudFront helps distribute traffic but does not provide the expert support needed.

text: A solutions architect is designing a secure architecture for a microservices application. Each microservice must be isolated in its own network segment with controlled inter-service communication. Which approach provides the BEST security isolation? (Select TWO)
options: Deploy each microservice in a separate VPC with VPC peering for communication
Use separate subnets for each microservice with Network ACLs controlling traffic
Deploy services in separate security groups with rules allowing specific inter-service communication
Implement AWS PrivateLink endpoints for service-to-service communication
Use a single security group with port-based rules for each microservice
explanation: Separate security groups per microservice provide microsegmentation with specific rules for inter-service communication. AWS PrivateLink creates private endpoints for service communication without traversing the public internet, providing additional security. Separate VPCs would be overly complex and expensive. Network ACLs are stateless and harder to manage for dynamic microservices. A single security group does not provide proper isolation.

text: A company needs to establish a secure, dedicated network connection between their on-premises data center and AWS VPC that bypasses the public internet. The connection must support consistent bandwidth and low latency for mission-critical applications. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Configure multiple Site-to-Site VPN connections for redundancy
Establish AWS Direct Connect with a dedicated network connection
Implement AWS Transit Gateway with VPN attachments
Use AWS PrivateLink with VPC endpoints
explanation: AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated network connection between on-premises and AWS that bypasses the public internet entirely. It offers consistent bandwidth, lower latency, and more predictable performance than internet-based connections. Site-to-Site VPN uses the internet and has variable performance. Transit Gateway facilitates connectivity but does not provide the dedicated connection. PrivateLink is for accessing AWS services privately, not for on-premises connectivity.

text: An application in a private subnet needs to access Amazon S3 and DynamoDB without traversing the internet. The solution must not require a NAT gateway and must keep all traffic within the AWS network. Which configuration meets these requirements?
options: Configure VPC endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB with appropriate route table entries
Set up AWS PrivateLink connections to S3 and DynamoDB
Implement AWS Direct Connect to access AWS services
Use VPC peering to connect to AWS service VPCs
explanation: VPC endpoints allow private subnet resources to access AWS services without internet access or NAT gateways. S3 and DynamoDB support gateway endpoints, which are free and require route table modifications. Traffic stays within the AWS network. PrivateLink is for interface endpoints, not available for S3 gateway access. Direct Connect is for on-premises connectivity. VPC peering does not provide service access.

text: A healthcare application must encrypt all data in transit between application components across multiple Availability Zones. The application uses Application Load Balancers and EC2 instances. Which combination of configurations ensures end-to-end encryption? (Select TWO)
options: Configure ALB listeners with SSL/TLS certificates from AWS Certificate Manager
Enable SSL/TLS termination at the ALB and use HTTP for backend connections
Configure target groups to use HTTPS health checks and traffic
Install SSL certificates on EC2 instances and configure applications for HTTPS
Use AWS Shield Advanced for encryption of inter-AZ traffic
explanation: ALB listeners should use ACM certificates for SSL/TLS termination at the load balancer. EC2 instances must also have SSL certificates installed and be configured for HTTPS to ensure end-to-end encryption from ALB to instances. Simply terminating SSL at the ALB leaves backend traffic unencrypted. HTTPS health checks alone do not encrypt traffic. Shield provides DDoS protection, not encryption.

text: A company wants to provide temporary access to private S3 objects for external partners without creating IAM users. The access must be time-limited and restricted to specific objects. Which solution is MOST secure?
options: Generate presigned URLs with expiration times for specific S3 objects
Create S3 bucket policies allowing access from partner IP addresses
Use Amazon Cognito identity pools to provide temporary credentials
Configure S3 Access Points with dedicated access policies for partners
explanation: Presigned URLs provide temporary, time-limited access to specific S3 objects without requiring AWS credentials. The URL includes a signature that validates the request and expires after a specified time. Bucket policies based on IP addresses are less secure and not time-limited. Cognito is overly complex for simple object sharing. S3 Access Points do not provide temporary access without credentials.

text: An application requires secure storage of database connection strings and API keys that must be automatically rotated every 60 days. The solution must integrate with RDS and provide audit trails of access. Which AWS service best meets these requirements?
options: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store with Lambda rotation function
AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation enabled
AWS Key Management Service with key rotation policies
Amazon DynamoDB with encryption and custom rotation logic
explanation: AWS Secrets Manager is purpose-built for storing and rotating secrets like database credentials. It provides native integration with RDS for automatic rotation, built-in rotation Lambda functions, and CloudTrail integration for audit trails. Parameter Store requires custom rotation logic. KMS manages encryption keys, not secrets. DynamoDB is not designed for secret management.

text: A company wants to automatically remediate security findings from Amazon GuardDuty. When GuardDuty detects compromised EC2 instances, the system should isolate the instance, capture forensic data, and notify the security team. Which architecture accomplishes this automation?
options: GuardDuty → CloudWatch Events → Lambda → EC2 API calls for isolation and SNS for notification
GuardDuty → AWS Config Rules → Systems Manager Automation → Security Hub
GuardDuty → CloudTrail → CloudWatch Alarms → Auto Scaling actions
GuardDuty → Direct EC2 termination → CloudFormation stack update
explanation: GuardDuty findings generate CloudWatch Events (EventBridge) that can trigger Lambda functions. Lambda can use EC2 APIs to isolate instances (modify security groups), create snapshots for forensics, and send SNS notifications. This provides automated response to threats. Config Rules do not directly integrate with GuardDuty findings. CloudTrail logs events but does not trigger automated responses. GuardDuty does not directly terminate instances.

text: A multi-tier application processes sensitive customer data. The architecture must ensure that the database tier can only be accessed from the application tier, the application tier can only be accessed from the web tier, and each tier must be able to download security patches from the internet. Which network design provides the MOST secure implementation?
options: Place all tiers in private subnets with a single NAT gateway, use security groups for tier isolation
Place web tier in public subnets, app and database tiers in separate private subnets with separate NAT gateways, use both security groups and NACLs
Place web tier in public subnets with IGW, app tier in private subnets with NAT gateway, database tier in private subnets without NAT, use VPC endpoints for updates
Place all tiers in public subnets with security groups providing access control between tiers
explanation: Option C provides the most secure design. The web tier in public subnets can receive traffic, the app tier in private subnets with NAT can fetch updates, and the database tier without NAT has maximum isolation. VPC endpoints can provide access to AWS services for patches without internet exposure. This design minimizes attack surface while maintaining necessary connectivity.

text: A company is deploying a web application that must protect against OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities, detect account compromise attempts, and automatically discover sensitive data exposure. Which combination of AWS services provides comprehensive security coverage? (Select THREE)
options: AWS WAF with AWS Managed Rules for OWASP Top 10 protection
Amazon GuardDuty for threat detection and account compromise monitoring
Amazon Macie for sensitive data discovery in S3
AWS Shield Standard for application vulnerability protection
Amazon Inspector for runtime vulnerability detection
AWS Config for security misconfiguration detection
explanation: AWS WAF with managed rules specifically protects against OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities. GuardDuty uses ML to detect threats including account compromise attempts. Macie automatically discovers and classifies sensitive data in S3. Shield protects against DDoS, not application vulnerabilities. Inspector is good for vulnerability assessment but does not cover all requirements. Config tracks configurations but does not detect account compromise.

text: A company needs to implement a Zero Trust network architecture for their AWS workloads. Applications should not trust any network traffic by default, and all communications must be authenticated and encrypted. Which design approach best implements Zero Trust principles?
options: Implement security groups with default deny rules and explicit allow rules for specific traffic
Deploy AWS Network Firewall with strict ingress and egress rules for all VPCs
Use AWS PrivateLink for all service communications and implement mutual TLS authentication
Place all resources in private subnets with NAT gateways for outbound access
explanation: Zero Trust requires never trusting any connection and always verifying. AWS PrivateLink provides private connectivity without internet exposure, and mutual TLS ensures both parties authenticate each other and encrypt traffic. This implements true Zero Trust. Security groups alone do not provide authentication. Network Firewall helps but does not ensure authentication. Private subnets improve security but do not implement Zero Trust principles.

text: An application handles credit card transactions and must comply with PCI DSS requirements. The application must log all access attempts, encrypt cardholder data, and implement network segmentation. Which combination of services meets these requirements? (Select THREE)
options: AWS CloudTrail for API logging and VPC Flow Logs for network traffic logging
AWS KMS for encryption key management and data encryption
Network ACLs and security groups for network segmentation
AWS WAF for logging web requests and blocking malicious traffic
Amazon CloudWatch Logs for centralized log aggregation
Separate VPCs for each application tier with Transit Gateway connectivity
explanation: CloudTrail and VPC Flow Logs provide comprehensive logging of API calls and network traffic for PCI compliance. KMS provides encryption key management with audit trails. Network ACLs and security groups implement required network segmentation. WAF is helpful but not required for basic PCI compliance. CloudWatch Logs is useful but the logging sources are more critical. Separate VPCs would be overly complex for PCI segmentation requirements.

text: A company needs to provide secure remote access for administrators to manage EC2 instances in private subnets. The solution must not expose RDP/SSH ports to the internet and must provide session logging for compliance. Which solution is MOST secure?
options: Deploy a bastion host in a public subnet with security group restrictions
Implement AWS Systems Manager Session Manager for instance access
Configure AWS Client VPN with MFA authentication
Set up AWS Direct Connect for administrator access
explanation: Systems Manager Session Manager provides secure shell access without opening inbound ports, exposing bastion hosts, or managing SSH keys. It logs all sessions to CloudTrail and S3 for compliance. Bastion hosts require exposing SSH/RDP ports and managing additional infrastructure. Client VPN requires more complex setup and still needs open ports on instances. Direct Connect is for site-to-site connectivity, not individual administrator access.

text: A financial services company must ensure their VPC traffic to AWS services never traverses the public internet. They use multiple AWS services including S3, DynamoDB, Lambda, and RDS. Which solution provides private connectivity to ALL these services?
options: Configure VPC Gateway Endpoints for all services
Implement AWS PrivateLink with Interface Endpoints for each service
Use a combination of Gateway Endpoints for S3/DynamoDB and Interface Endpoints for other services
Set up AWS Direct Connect with Virtual Interfaces to each service
explanation: S3 and DynamoDB support Gateway Endpoints (free, route-table based), while Lambda and RDS require Interface Endpoints (using PrivateLink technology). This combination provides private connectivity to all services. Gateway Endpoints are not available for Lambda/RDS. Not all services support the same endpoint type. Direct Connect provides private connectivity to AWS but does not eliminate the need for VPC endpoints for private service access.

text: A SaaS application must support multi-tenant isolation where each customer data is completely separated. The application runs on ECS with RDS databases. Which approach provides the STRONGEST tenant isolation?
options: Single ECS cluster with task-level IAM roles and single RDS instance with schema separation
Separate ECS services per tenant in one cluster with separate RDS databases
Separate AWS accounts per tenant with AWS Organizations management
Single shared infrastructure with application-level tenant filtering
explanation: Separate AWS accounts per tenant provides the strongest isolation boundary. Each tenant has completely isolated resources, IAM policies, and blast radius limitation. AWS Organizations enables centralized management. Other options rely on logical separation which could be compromised by misconfigurations or vulnerabilities. Account-level isolation is the strongest form of multi-tenant security in AWS.

text: A web application is experiencing sophisticated bot attacks that bypass traditional rate limiting. The bots rotate IP addresses and mimic human behavior. Which solution provides the MOST effective protection?
options: Implement AWS WAF with rate-based rules and IP reputation lists
Deploy AWS WAF with AWS Bot Control managed rule group
Configure CloudFront with custom Lambda@Edge functions for bot detection
Use Amazon GuardDuty to detect and block bot traffic
explanation: AWS WAF Bot Control uses machine learning and fingerprinting techniques to detect sophisticated bots that rotate IPs and mimic human behavior. It identifies bot signatures beyond simple rate limiting. Basic WAF rate rules are insufficient for sophisticated bots. Lambda@Edge requires custom bot detection logic. GuardDuty detects threats but does not block web traffic directly.

text: An application stores sensitive documents in S3 that must be encrypted with customer-managed keys. The company requires separate encryption keys per department, automatic key rotation, and detailed audit logs of key usage. Which solution meets all requirements?
options: S3 Server-Side Encryption with Customer-Provided Keys (SSE-C)
S3 Server-Side Encryption with AWS KMS Customer Master Keys (SSE-KMS) with separate keys per department
S3 Client-Side Encryption with keys stored in AWS Secrets Manager
S3 Default Encryption with S3-Managed Keys (SSE-S3) and bucket policies per department
explanation: SSE-KMS with customer-managed CMKs allows creating separate keys per department, enables automatic key rotation (annually), and provides detailed CloudTrail logs of key usage. SSE-C requires managing key rotation manually and does not provide AWS audit logs. Client-side encryption increases application complexity. SSE-S3 uses AWS-managed keys without department separation or detailed audit logs.

text: A company needs to implement defense in depth for a critical web application. Which combination of security controls provides comprehensive protection at different layers? (Select THREE)
options: CloudFront with AWS Shield Standard for DDoS protection at edge locations
AWS WAF attached to ALB for application layer filtering
Security groups and NACLs for network layer access control
Amazon Macie for real-time traffic analysis
VPC Flow Logs for threat detection
AWS Network Firewall for stateful traffic inspection
explanation: CloudFront with Shield provides edge-level DDoS protection. WAF on ALB filters application-layer attacks. Security groups and NACLs provide network-layer defense in depth with stateful and stateless filtering. Macie analyzes S3 data, not real-time traffic. VPC Flow Logs record traffic but do not detect threats. Network Firewall adds security but the three selected options provide comprehensive coverage at edge, application, and network layers.

text: A healthcare company must ensure their container workloads on ECS Fargate comply with security best practices. They need to scan container images for vulnerabilities, enforce least privilege access, and prevent containers from running as root. Which combination of services achieves these requirements? (Select TWO)
options: Amazon ECR with image scanning to detect vulnerabilities before deployment
Amazon Inspector to continuously scan running Fargate tasks
Configure task IAM roles with minimal required permissions
Use ECS task definitions with user namespaces to prevent root access
Implement AWS App Mesh for service-to-service authentication
explanation: ECR image scanning identifies vulnerabilities in container images before deployment, meeting the vulnerability scanning requirement. Task IAM roles provide least privilege access by granting only necessary permissions to each container. Inspector now supports Fargate but ECR scanning is more appropriate for pre-deployment checks. Fargate does not support user namespaces directly; non-root users must be configured in the container image. App Mesh provides service mesh capabilities but does not address the core security requirements.

text: A company stores sensitive financial data across multiple AWS services including S3, EBS volumes, and RDS databases. They need to implement encryption at rest using customer-managed keys with the ability to audit all key usage and implement automatic key rotation. Which solution provides the MOST comprehensive approach?
options: Enable default encryption on each service using AWS-managed keys
Implement AWS KMS customer-managed keys (CMKs) with key policies and automatic rotation enabled
Use AWS CloudHSM for all encryption operations with custom key management
Implement client-side encryption for all services using keys stored in Secrets Manager
explanation: AWS KMS with customer-managed CMKs provides centralized key management across all AWS services. It supports automatic annual rotation, detailed CloudTrail logging for audit trails, and key policies for fine-grained access control. AWS-managed keys do not provide the same level of control. CloudHSM is more complex and expensive for this use case. Client-side encryption increases application complexity unnecessarily.

text: A healthcare organization must ensure their RDS MySQL database containing patient records meets HIPAA compliance requirements. The data must be encrypted at rest and in transit, with encryption keys rotated annually. Which configuration meets ALL requirements?
options: Enable RDS encryption with AWS KMS CMK, force SSL connections, and enable automatic key rotation
Use Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) with RDS-managed keys and SSL certificates
Implement database-level encryption using MySQL native encryption with Secrets Manager
Configure RDS with default encryption and VPN connections for all database access
explanation: RDS encryption with KMS CMK provides encryption at rest with automatic annual rotation capability. Forcing SSL connections (requiring SSL in DB parameter group) ensures encryption in transit. This combination meets HIPAA requirements. TDE is not available for MySQL. MySQL native encryption does not integrate with AWS key management. VPN does not provide database-level encryption in transit.

text: An organization needs to implement encryption for EBS volumes attached to EC2 instances. They require different encryption keys for development and production environments with the ability to share encrypted snapshots with specific AWS accounts. Which approach meets these requirements? (Select TWO)
options: Create separate KMS CMKs for dev and prod environments with appropriate key policies
Use EBS default encryption with a single KMS key and IAM policies for access control
Configure EBS encryption by default at the account level with AWS-managed keys
Grant cross-account access through KMS key policies and share encrypted snapshots
Use EC2 instance store volumes with application-level encryption
explanation: Separate KMS CMKs for each environment provide isolation and compliance with different key requirements. KMS key policies can grant cross-account permissions, allowing encrypted snapshot sharing while maintaining encryption. Default encryption with one key does not provide environment separation. AWS-managed keys ca not be shared cross-account. Instance store volumes are ephemeral and inappropriate for persistent encrypted data.

text: A company microservices architecture requires end-to-end encryption for all service-to-service communication across multiple Availability Zones. The solution must support automatic certificate renewal and centralized certificate management. Which approach is MOST effective?
options: Implement AWS Certificate Manager with Application Load Balancers for all services
Use AWS Private Certificate Authority with ACM for internal service certificates
Configure self-signed certificates stored in Secrets Manager with Lambda rotation
Deploy AWS App Mesh with mutual TLS using ACM Private CA
explanation: AWS App Mesh with mTLS using ACM Private CA provides comprehensive service-to-service encryption. App Mesh automatically handles certificate distribution and renewal, while Private CA issues certificates for internal services. This provides end-to-end encryption with minimal operational overhead. ALBs alone do not provide service mesh capabilities. Self-signed certificates require complex rotation logic.

text: An application must encrypt data in transit between on-premises systems and AWS services including S3, RDS, and Lambda. The company requires certificate pinning and visibility into all encrypted traffic. Which solution provides the MOST secure implementation?
options: Configure Site-to-Site VPN with certificate authentication and VPC endpoints
Implement AWS Direct Connect with MACsec encryption and PrivateLink endpoints
Use Transit Gateway with AWS Network Firewall for traffic inspection
Configure API Gateway with mutual TLS for all service interactions
explanation: Direct Connect with MACsec provides Layer 2 encryption for the dedicated connection. Combined with PrivateLink endpoints, all traffic remains within AWS private network with encryption. This supports certificate requirements and allows traffic inspection at the Network Firewall level. VPN does not provide the same level of control. API Gateway does not cover all services mentioned.

text: A financial services company requires encryption keys to be rotated every 90 days for PCI DSS compliance. They use multiple AWS services and need centralized key management with automatic rotation. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Enable automatic key rotation in AWS KMS (rotates annually) and implement manual quarterly rotation
Use AWS Secrets Manager with custom Lambda functions for 90-day key rotation
Implement AWS CloudHSM with custom key rotation automation
Create new KMS CMKs every 90 days using CloudWatch Events and Lambda
explanation: KMS automatic rotation is annual and cannot be customized to 90 days. Creating new CMKs every 90 days with Lambda automation meets the requirement. Old keys remain available for decryption while new keys are used for encryption. Secrets Manager is for secrets/credentials, not encryption keys. CloudHSM requires complex custom automation.

text: An organization needs to implement a key hierarchy where data encryption keys (DEKs) are encrypted by key encryption keys (KEKs), with strict separation of duties. Cryptographic operations must be performed in FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated hardware. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: AWS KMS with customer-managed CMKs and envelope encryption
AWS CloudHSM cluster with custom key hierarchy implementation
AWS KMS with AWS-managed keys and client-side encryption
AWS Secrets Manager with KMS integration for key storage
explanation: AWS CloudHSM provides FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated HSMs and allows complete control over key hierarchy implementation. You can implement DEK/KEK separation with custom policies. KMS uses FIPS 140-2 Level 2 validation. Secrets Manager is not designed for cryptographic key hierarchies.

text: A company needs to implement fine-grained access control for their data lake in S3, with different teams having access to specific prefixes and object tags. The solution must provide centralized access management and detailed audit logging. Which approach is MOST appropriate? (Select TWO)
options: Implement AWS Lake Formation with data permissions and column-level security
Use S3 bucket policies with conditions based on object tags and prefixes
Configure IAM policies with S3 resource-level permissions for each team
Create separate S3 buckets for each team with cross-account access
Use S3 Access Points with custom access policies for each team
explanation: Lake Formation provides centralized data governance with fine-grained permissions including column-level security for data lakes. S3 Access Points provide dedicated endpoints with custom policies for different access patterns, simplifying complex permission scenarios. Bucket policies alone become complex with many teams. IAM policies have size limits. Separate buckets increase management overhead.

text: A healthcare company must ensure that patient data in S3 is automatically classified, encrypted with specific keys based on sensitivity, and archived after 7 years for compliance. Which combination of services achieves these requirements? (Select THREE)
options: Amazon Macie for automatic data classification and sensitivity detection
S3 Intelligent-Tiering for automatic data archival after 7 years
S3 Lifecycle policies to transition data to Glacier after 7 years
S3 Object Lambda to dynamically encrypt objects based on classification
AWS KMS with different CMKs for each data classification level
S3 Batch Operations to apply encryption after classification
explanation: Macie automatically discovers and classifies sensitive data. S3 Lifecycle policies can transition objects to Glacier after 7 years for compliant archival. Different KMS CMKs per classification level provide appropriate encryption. Intelligent-Tiering optimizes storage costs but does not archive based on time. Object Lambda transforms data on retrieval, not for encryption at rest. Batch Operations could work but is less automated than lifecycle policies.

text: A company requires automated backups of their entire AWS environment including EC2 instances, RDS databases, and EFS file systems. Backups must be encrypted, replicated to another region, and retained according to a grandfather-father-son rotation scheme. Which solution provides the MOST comprehensive approach?
options: AWS Backup with cross-region backup copies and custom lifecycle policies
Individual service backup features with Lambda orchestration
AWS Systems Manager Maintenance Windows with custom backup scripts
Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager for all resource backups
explanation: AWS Backup provides centralized backup across AWS services with native support for EC2, RDS, and EFS. It supports encrypted backups, cross-region replication, and complex retention policies including GFS rotation schemes. Individual service features lack centralized management. Systems Manager Maintenance Windows are not designed for comprehensive backup. DLM only handles EBS volumes.

text: An organization needs to implement point-in-time recovery for their DynamoDB tables containing transaction data. They require the ability to restore to any second within the last 30 days and replicate data to another region for disaster recovery. Which configuration meets these requirements?
options: Enable DynamoDB point-in-time recovery and create periodic backup copies
Configure DynamoDB continuous backups with global tables for multi-region replication
Implement DynamoDB Streams with Lambda to backup to S3
Use AWS Backup for DynamoDB with cross-region replication
explanation: DynamoDB continuous backups (PITR) allows restoration to any second within 35 days. Global Tables provide active-active multi-region replication for disaster recovery. This combination meets all requirements. Periodic backups do not provide point-in-time granularity. Streams with Lambda is complex and does not provide built-in PITR. AWS Backup for DynamoDB provides daily snapshots, not continuous PITR.

text: A media company stores petabytes of video content in S3. They need to automatically classify content by access patterns, minimize storage costs, and ensure frequently accessed content remains immediately available. Compliance requires 11 9s durability for all content. Which solution is MOST cost-effective?
options: Implement S3 Intelligent-Tiering with all optional archive tiers enabled
Use S3 Analytics to identify patterns and manually create lifecycle policies
Configure S3 Standard for hot data and Glacier Flexible Retrieval for archives
Deploy S3 Lifecycle policies based on object tags and last access time
explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between access tiers based on access patterns without retrieval fees. It maintains 11 9s durability across all tiers and keeps frequently accessed data immediately available. Manual lifecycle management is operationally complex. Standard to Glacier transitions require predicting access patterns. Lifecycle policies based on last access time are not natively supported.

text: A global financial institution must comply with data residency requirements where customer data cannot leave specific geographic regions. They need to prevent accidental cross-region data transfers while maintaining global application functionality. Which controls should they implement? (Select TWO)
options: S3 bucket policies with aws:RequestedRegion condition to restrict access by region
AWS Organizations SCPs to prevent resource creation outside approved regions
VPC endpoint policies to restrict data transfer to specific regions
IAM permission boundaries to limit user actions to specific regions
AWS Config rules to detect and remediate cross-region transfers
explanation: Organizations SCPs can prevent resource creation and API calls outside approved regions at the organization level. IAM permission boundaries provide an additional layer restricting the maximum permissions users can have to specific regions. S3 bucket policies with RequestedRegion only control where requests originate, not data residency. VPC endpoints do not prevent cross-region transfers. Config can detect but not prevent transfers.

text: A healthcare provider must implement HIPAA-compliant audit logging for all data access to patient records stored across S3, RDS, and DynamoDB. Logs must be tamper-proof, encrypted, and retained for 6 years. Which architecture meets these requirements?
options: CloudTrail with S3 Object Lock and CloudWatch Logs Insights for analysis
CloudTrail logging to S3 with MFA delete, KMS encryption, and Lifecycle policies
CloudTrail with log file integrity validation, S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode, and SSE-KMS
VPC Flow Logs and database audit logs aggregated in CloudWatch Logs
explanation: CloudTrail with integrity validation ensures logs have not been tampered with. S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode makes logs immutable for 6 years. SSE-KMS provides encryption at rest. This combination meets all HIPAA logging requirements. MFA delete alone does not provide immutability. VPC Flow Logs do not capture application-level data access.

text: A company runs multiple web applications behind Application Load Balancers. They need to implement SSL/TLS certificates that automatically renew, support multiple domain names, and provide certificate transparency logs. Which solution requires the LEAST operational overhead?
options: AWS Certificate Manager public certificates with automatic renewal
Lets Encrypt certificates with Lambda-based renewal automation
AWS Private Certificate Authority with ACM Private CA
Self-signed certificates stored in Secrets Manager with rotation
explanation: ACM public certificates are free, automatically renew, support multiple domains via SAN, and provide certificate transparency logs. They integrate natively with ALB with zero operational overhead. Lets Encrypt requires custom automation. Private CA is for internal certificates and has costs. Self-signed certificates require manual management.

text: An enterprise requires internal applications to use certificates from their existing PKI infrastructure while cloud-native applications use AWS-managed certificates. They need centralized certificate lifecycle management. Which architecture meets these requirements? (Select TWO)
options: Import third-party certificates into ACM for internal applications
Deploy AWS Private Certificate Authority as a subordinate CA to existing PKI
Use ACM public certificates for all applications
Configure IAM as a certificate authority for internal certificates
Implement certificate connector for Active Directory Certificate Services
explanation: Importing third-party certificates into ACM allows centralized management while maintaining existing PKI. Private CA as subordinate to existing PKI extends the trust chain into AWS while preserving existing infrastructure. Public certificates would not work for internal applications.
